1	# ADDPlus+ — Nairobi's Collective SME Marketplace
2	
3	> One M-Pesa payment. Multiple vendors. Funds held until you say so.
4	
5	ADDPlus+ is a multi-vendor marketplace built specifically for Nairobi's informal and semi-formal SME ecosystem — fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, and fragrance — unified under one roof with escrow-backed payments, compliance scoring, and a collective advancement fund.
6	
7	**Document type:** Principal Architect forensic README — Single Source of Truth for Senior Engineering / CTO.  
8	**Repository:** `addplus-platform` monorepo (npm workspaces)  
9	**Last forensic audit:** 2026-06-23 `[UPDATED]` — Principal Architect + Technical Historian + Global Scalability Auditor pass (re-verification of HEAD `62b96c4`; no application code changes since 2026-06-16)  
10	**Git history:** 77 commits (first commit 2026-03-19; HEAD `62b96c4`)  
11	**Source files:** 125 TypeScript/TSX files under `apps/` (excluding `node_modules`)  
12	**API surface:** 84 route handlers across 10 route modules · 22 Prisma models · 11 service modules  
13	**Web surface:** 31 `page.tsx` routes · 19 shared components · 7 Zustand stores  
14	**Automated tests:** **None** — 0 test files across entire monorepo  
15	**Production:** Web [addplus.vercel.app](https://addplus.vercel.app) · API [addplus-api.onrender.com](https://addplus-api.onrender.com) · DB Turso `addplus-db`
16	
17	### Audit Executive Summary (2026-06-23, excl. payment/checkout E2E)
18	
19	| Status | Scope |
20	|--------|--------|
21	| ✅ **Working** | Password auth (web + mobile); vendor registration + dashboard CRUD; admin overview/vendors/orders/disputes/insights (13 admin endpoints); public vendor directory + storefronts; marketplace catalog from Turso with **in-page API search**; order creation + STK initiation API; `mpesa_request_id` persistence on pay; Cloudinary uploads; Render+Vercel+Turso deploy pipeline; `/account/orders` confirm-delivery/dispute wired with **order item IDs** |
22	| ⚠️ **Partial** | Homepage/marketplace mock ratings & reviews; cart promos/shipping UI (not sent to API); order tracking page; vendor store photo upload variant; admin fund balance (`DATE_TRUNC` SQL); mobile API+mock hybrid + **mobile cart fail-open**; compliance referral URL-only; web cart checkout shows errors (no fake success) but payment E2E unverified; marketplace ignores URL `?search=` / `?category=` deep links |
23	| 🔴 **Not working** | Payment/checkout E2E (M-Pesa signature stub, B2C ref mismatch); OTP (disabled); customer registration page; `/flash-sales`; navbar desktop search; wishlist hearts on listing grids; stock not decremented on order; fund monthly trend SQL on Turso; automated tests (0) |
24	
25	Official admin/vendor account: **`254115594826`** (role `admin`, linked Bliss Veggies store). First login may require password setup via web.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Table of Contents
30	
31	1. [Genesis & Evolution](#1-genesis--evolution) `[UPDATED 2026-06-23]`
32	2. [Core Architecture](#2-core-architecture) `[UPDATED 2026-06-23]`
33	3. [Functional Deep-Dive](#3-functional-deep-dive) `[UPDATED 2026-06-23]`
34	4. [Feature Audit & Production Readiness Assessment](#4-feature-audit--production-readiness-assessment) `[UPDATED 2026-06-23]`
35	5. [Known Issues & Technical Debt](#5-known-issues--technical-debt) `[UPDATED 2026-06-23]`
36	6. [Missing Features — Global Standards Gap Analysis](#6-missing-features--global-standards-gap-analysis)
37	7. [Conception to Current State](#7-conception-to-current-state) `[UPDATED 2026-06-23]`
38	8. [Quick Reference](#8-quick-reference)
39

41	
42	## 1. Genesis & Evolution
43	
44	### 1.1 Original Problem Statement
45	
46	ADDPlus+ was conceived to solve a specific Nairobi SME pain point: informal vendors (fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, fragrance) sell on fragmented channels (WhatsApp, Instagram, physical stalls) with no unified checkout, no buyer protection, and no collective bargaining power. The platform's core thesis:
47	
48	- **One cart, many vendors** — customer pays once via M-Pesa
49	- **Escrow** — funds held until buyer confirms delivery (or auto-release after timeout)
50	- **10% transaction levy** — split 5% to a collective advancement fund + 5% to platform profit share
51	- **Compliance scoring** — vendors earn visibility through daily posts and referral activity
52	
53	**Pre-repository concept notes:** Data Unavailable — no concept documents exist prior to the first git commit. The earliest written product intent is in `docs/PRD.md` and `docs/PRD_SHORT.md`, added in commit `5c131bc` (2026-04-15).
54	
55	### 1.2 First Commit (2026-03-19)
56	
57	**Commit:** `49abff0` — `Initial commit: ADDPlus+ platform with comprehensive security`  
58	**Author:** Ken.M
59	
60	The repository launched as a full monorepo on day one:
61	
62	| Decision | Choice | Rationale (inferred from code + commits) |
63	|----------|--------|------------------------------------------|
64	| Monorepo | npm workspaces (`apps/*`, `packages/*`) | Share types, coordinate web/mobile/API releases |
65	| Web | Next.js 14 App Router | SSR/SSG for SEO, Vercel-native deployment |
66	| Mobile | React Native + Expo SDK 50 | Single codebase for Android APK via EAS |
67	| API | Node.js + Express + TypeScript | Familiar stack, fast iteration for Kenyan fintech patterns |
68	| ORM | Prisma + Turso/libSQL (SQLite dialect) | Type-safe queries; production via `@prisma/adapter-libsql` |
69	| Cache | Redis | OTP rate limiting, JWT blacklist, user cache |
70	| Payments | Safaricom M-Pesa Daraja | Dominant mobile money in Kenya; STK Push + B2C for vendor payouts |
71	| SMS/OTP | Africa's Talking | Local SMS provider for Kenyan numbers |
72	| Images | Cloudinary | CDN + auto-optimization for vendor product photos |
73	
74	**Alternatives not chosen (Data Unavailable for explicit rejection rationale):** Firebase, Supabase Auth, Stripe (not Kenya-native), Flutter, TurboRepo (attempted then removed).
75	
76	### 1.3 Chronological Evolution (Every Major Pivot)
77

781	#### 3.2.4 Auth Flow (API — June 2026)
782	
783	```
784	POST /v1/auth/login { phone, password }
785	  → normalize phone to 254XXXXXXXXX
786	  → bcrypt.compare against User.password_hash
787	  → if no hash and role admin/vendor → { needsPasswordSetup: true }
788	  → JWT access (HS256, 15m) + refresh token (UUID, 7d in DB)
789	  → response includes vendor_profile_id when VendorProfile exists (any role)
790	
791	POST /v1/auth/password/setup { phone, password }
792	  → bcrypt hash → User.password_hash (admin/vendor first-time)
793	
794	POST /v1/auth/register { phone, password, role: vendor }
795	  → create User with password_hash
796	
797	POST /v1/auth/otp/* (only if ENABLE_OTP_AUTH=true)
798	  → otherwise 503 Service Unavailable
799	
800	Protected routes → Bearer JWT
801	  → Redis blacklist check (optional)
802	  → Redis user cache (5m) or DB fallback
803	  → authorize('vendor', 'admin') on vendor self-service routes
804	```

808	#### 3.2.5 Business Logic: Escrow & Levies
809	
810	On successful STK callback:
811	1. Order status → `confirmed`
812	2. Per order item: `EscrowLedger` created with status `held`
813	3. 5% → `CollectiveFund` (advancement_contribution)
814	4. 5% → profit_share_contribution pool
815	5. Net amount held for vendor
816	
817	On delivery confirm or cron auto-release:
818	1. Deduct `fine_balance` from vendor payout
819	2. B2C to vendor `mpesa_number` if net ≥ KES 500
820	3. Escrow status → `released`
821	
822	**Escrow auto-release path:** `auto_release_at` is set in `updateOrderItemStatus` when status=`dispatched` (+48h). **Gap:** not set at payment confirmation — if vendor never dispatches, cron in `crons.ts` never matches and escrow stays held indefinitely.

1284	**The Problem (Conceptual — Early 2024 per PROJECT_PROGRESS.md, pre-git)**  
1285	Nairobi's informal SMEs sell in isolation. Buyers trust individual vendors on WhatsApp but fear paying strangers. Vendors lack scale. No platform combined multi-vendor checkout with M-Pesa escrow and a cooperative fund. ADDPlus+ was designed to be that platform.
1286	
1287	**Day Zero (2026-03-19)**  
1288	Ken.M committed the entire platform skeleton in one shot: Express API with Prisma schema covering users, vendors, products, orders, escrow, compliance, collective fund, importation, disputes, grants; Next.js web with marketplace, cart, vendor pages; Expo mobile with core screens; security middleware from the start. The architectural bet was **monorepo + M-Pesa-native + escrow-first** — not a generic Shopify clone.

1290	**The Deployment Struggle (2026-03-27 — 2026-04-11)**  
1291	Two weeks of commits fought Vercel: API build attempts, turbo removal, workspace script fixes. The outcome: **web deploys to Vercel; API intended for Railway/similar** (per `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`). # ADDPlus+ — Nairobi's Collective SME Marketplace

> One M-Pesa payment. Multiple vendors. Funds held until you say so.

ADDPlus+ is a multi-vendor marketplace built specifically for Nairobi's informal and semi-formal SME ecosystem — fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, and fragrance — unified under one roof with escrow-backed payments, compliance scoring, and a collective advancement fund.

## 1. Genesis & Evolution

### 1.1 Original Problem Statement

ADDPlus+ was conceived to solve a specific Nairobi SME pain point: informal vendors (fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, fragrance) sell on fragmented channels (WhatsApp, Instagram, physical stalls) with no unified checkout, no buyer protection, and no collective bargaining power. The platform's core thesis:

- **One cart, many vendors** — customer pays once via M-Pesa
- **Escrow** — funds held until buyer confirms delivery (or auto-release after timeout)
- **10% transaction levy** — split 5% to a collective advancement fund + 5% to platform profit share
- **Compliance scoring** — vendors earn visibility through daily posts and referral activity

### 1.4 Architectural Decision Records

#### ADR-001: Mock-First Development → **Superseded (June 2026)**
**Status:** Partially retired  
Catalog and dashboards now call live API (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://addplus-api.onrender.com/v1`). `mockData.ts` **catalog arrays are empty** (`MOCK_PRODUCTS`, `MOCK_VENDORS`, `MOCK_ORDERS = []`). **Still active** for: product ratings, reviews, Q&A, variants, promo codes, shipping/pickup UI, order tracking timeline, mobile fallbacks.

#### ADR-002: Auth — Password Primary, OTP Disabled
**Status:** Active (June 2026)  
Web/mobile use `POST /v1/auth/login` (phone + password). OTP routes return **503** unless `ENABLE_OTP_AUTH=true` + Africa's Talking configured. Session cookies via `/api/auth/session` (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, `user_role` httpOnly). Demo tokens (`demo-token-*`) rejected by middleware.

#### ADR-003: Zustand over Redux/Context
**Status:** Active  
Cart, wishlist, compare, auth (mobile) use Zustand with `persist` middleware → `localStorage` (web) / `AsyncStorage` (mobile). Survives refresh; no server-side cart sync.

#### ADR-004: React Navigation over Expo Router (Mobile)
**Status:** Active  
Explicit stack + bottom-tab navigation in `App.tsx`. No file-based routing.

#### ADR-005: Prisma over Raw SQL
**Status:** Active  
All DB access through Prisma Client. `migration_fix_schema.sql` exists as manual backup but Prisma migrations are canonical.

#### ADR-006: No Turborepo
**Status:** Active  
Removed after Vercel CI conflicts. Root `package.json` scripts delegate to workspaces directly.

#### ADR-007: Homepage Design Freeze
**Status:** Active (per design requirements)  
May 2026 redesign updated marketplace, vendors, cart, login, vendor pages — **homepage layout intentionally preserved**.

#### ADR-008: Brand Color Constraint
**Status:** Active  
Primary green `#22C55E` (updated from `#1DB954`). **Never use pink `#ec4899`** anywhere in codebase.

### 2.5 API Middleware Stack (Execution Order)

1. `helmet` — CSP, HSTS, referrer policy
2. `cors` — `CLIENT_URL` origin, credentials enabled
3. `express-rate-limit` — global 100 req / 15 min
4. `express.json` — 1 MB body limit
5. `express.urlencoded` — 1 MB, 1000 param limit
6. `requestLogger` — structured AUDIT JSON + requestId
7. Route-specific: `authLimiter` (5/15min) on `/v1/auth`, `/v1/admin`
8. ~~Route-specific: `paymentLimiter`~~ — **defined in `server.ts` but NOT mounted** on `/v1/payments` (webhooks intentionally unthrottled)
9. Per-route `validateInput` — threat detection + sanitization
10. Per-route `authenticate` + `authorize(roles)`
11. `errorHandler` — AppError/Zod/Prisma mapping
12. 404 handler

**Defined but unused:** `paymentLimiter` (10/hr — not mounted), `uploadLimiter` (5/hr — not mounted on `/v1/uploads`), `verifyOwnership`, `ipWhitelist`, `validateFileUpload`

**Render production flags (`render.yaml`):** `AUTO_APPROVE_VENDORS=true` — vendors skip manual KYC gate on registration in production; `ENABLE_OTP_AUTH=false`; `EXPOSE_DEV_OTP=false`.

### 2.6 Cron Jobs (`apps/api/src/jobs/crons.ts`)

| Job | Schedule | Behavior |
|-----|----------|----------|
| Escrow auto-release | `*/30 * * * *` | Release held escrow where `auto_release_at <= now` — **⚠️ `auto_release_at` set only when vendor marks `dispatched` (+48h); never at payment; if vendor never dispatches, cron never fires** |
| Daily compliance scoring | `55 23 * * *` | Score all approved vendors; issue fines; update 7-day rolling `compliance_score` |
| Weekly profit-share | `0 6 * * 1` | Distribute `profit_share_contribution` pool via B2C proportional to weekly sales |

// apps/web/src/store/useCartStore.ts
addItem: (item) => {
  const existing = get().items.find(
    (i) => i.productId === item.productId && i.variantId === item.variantId
  )
  if (existing) {
    set((s) => ({
      items: s.items.map((i) =>
        i.productId === item.productId && i.variantId === item.variantId
          ? { ...i, qty: i.qty + 1 } : i
      ),
    }))
  } else {
    set((s) => ({ items: [...s.items, { ...item, qty: 1 }] }))
  }
},

#### 3.2.4 Auth Flow (API — June 2026)

```
POST /v1/auth/login { phone, password }
  → normalize phone to 254XXXXXXXXX
  → bcrypt.compare against User.password_hash
  → if no hash and role admin/vendor → { needsPasswordSetup: true }
  → JWT access (HS256, 15m) + refresh token (UUID, 7d in DB)
  → response includes vendor_profile_id when VendorProfile exists (any role)

POST /v1/auth/password/setup { phone, password }
  → bcrypt hash → User.password_hash (admin/vendor first-time)

POST /v1/auth/register { phone, password, role: vendor }
  → create User with password_hash

POST /v1/auth/otp/* (only if ENABLE_OTP_AUTH=true)
  → otherwise 503 Service Unavailable

Protected routes → Bearer JWT
  → Redis blacklist check (optional)
  → Redis user cache (5m) or DB fallback
  → authorize('vendor', 'admin') on vendor self-service routes
```

**Image uploads (`apps/api/src/lib/imageUpload.ts`):** Cloudinary when `CLOUDINARY_*` set (Render production); else ephemeral disk on Render free tier (lost on redeploy).

#### 3.2.5 Business Logic: Escrow & Levies

On successful STK callback:
1. Order status → `confirmed`
2. Per order item: `EscrowLedger` created with status `held`
3. 5% → `CollectiveFund` (advancement_contribution)
4. 5% → profit_share_contribution pool
5. Net amount held for vendor

On delivery confirm or cron auto-release:
1. Deduct `fine_balance` from vendor payout
2. B2C to vendor `mpesa_number` if net ≥ KES 500
3. Escrow status → `released`

**Escrow auto-release path:** `auto_release_at` is set in `updateOrderItemStatus` when status=`dispatched` (+48h). **Gap:** not set at payment confirmation — if vendor never dispatches, cron in `crons.ts` never matches and escrow stays held indefinitely.

## 7. Conception to Current State `[UPDATED]`

### 7.1 Narrative Timeline

**The Problem (Conceptual — Early 2024 per PROJECT_PROGRESS.md, pre-git)**  
Nairobi's informal SMEs sell in isolation. Buyers trust individual vendors on WhatsApp but fear paying strangers. Vendors lack scale. No platform combined multi-vendor checkout with M-Pesa escrow and a cooperative fund. ADDPlus+ was designed to be that platform.

**Day Zero (2026-03-19)**  
Ken.M committed the entire platform skeleton in one shot: Express API with Prisma schema covering users, vendors, products, orders, escrow, compliance, collective fund, importation, disputes, grants; Next.js web with marketplace, cart, vendor pages; Expo mobile with core screens; security middleware from the start. The architectural bet was **monorepo + M-Pesa-native + escrow-first** — not a generic Shopify clone.

**The Deployment Struggle (2026-03-27 — 2026-04-11)**  
Two weeks of commits fought Vercel: API build attempts, turbo removal, workspace script fixes. The outcome: **web deploys to Vercel; API intended for Railway/similar** (per `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`). Turborepo was rejected after CI sandbox conflicts — a lesson that tooling choices must match deployment target constraints.

**Phase 0-1 (2026-04-03)**  
Business logic landed: OTP auth service, escrow ledger, compliance scoring, importation STK deposits, Redis integration, cron jobs. This is the "backend complete" milestone — but **complete means code exists**, not that it runs in production with real data.

**The Mock Pivot (2026-04-11 — 2026-04-15)**  
The most important product decision: **mock data fallback on API failure**. This let Vercel host a fully browsable marketplace without a live API. Auth was simplified to phone-only demo login. Mobile got the same treatment plus EAS/GitHub Actions for APK builds. Documentation suite written — PRD, architecture, business logic — institutionalizing the vision for future developers.

**Framework Upgrade (2026-04-23)**  
Next.js 14 → 15.2.8 for security and async dynamic route params. `vercel.json` settled at repo root with hoisted React deps. Production polish: OG meta, 404 page, loading skeletons.

**The Feature Parity Sprint (2026-05-11)**  
In a single day, ~20 commits added: Sellfy/Amazon UI redesign, product variants, shipping options, Kenyan features (COD, WhatsApp, flash sales, pickup stations, boda boda), compare, quick view, save for later, back in stock, size guide, photo reviews, security hardening, production readiness documentation. The frontend reached ~90% feature parity with Jumia/Kilimall patterns. The backend remained at ~10% operational readiness because **integration was never completed**.

**Current State (June 2026 — post password-auth + Turso deploy + forensic audits)**  
- **Web:** [addplus.vercel.app](https://addplus.vercel.app) — live catalog, vendor/admin dashboards, password auth. Mock enrichment for reviews/ratings/shipping. Web checkout calls real API; payment E2E unverified.  
- **API:** [addplus-api.onrender.com](https://addplus-api.onrender.com) on Render free tier (Frankfurt); Turso `addplus-db`; Cloudinary; OTP disabled; `AUTO_APPROVE_VENDORS=true`. 84 handlers; escrow/payment wiring bugs remain.  
- **Admin:** `254115594826` — same account operates admin console **and** Bliss Veggies vendor store (`vendor_profile_id` in JWT).  
- **Mobile:** Real `authApi.login`; API-first with mock fallbacks on 6 screens; **cart fail-open**; no admin UI; EAS assets still missing.  
- **Tests:** None.  
- **Integration:** ~**68%** for non-payment flows (up from 65% — confirm-delivery + mpesa_request_id fixes); **~18%** for payment E2E (up from 15% — web cart no longer fakes success).  
- **Global readiness score:** **33/100** (see §4.11) — marginal improvement from 32/100; multi-region, compliance, observability gaps unchanged.

import { sqliteTable, text, integer } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";

export const plans = sqliteTable("plans", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  name: text("name").notNull(),
  description: text("description"),
  priceKesMonthly: integer("price_kes_monthly"),
  priceUsdMonthly: integer("price_usd_monthly"),
  maxBranches: integer("max_branches").notNull().default(1),
  maxUsers: integer("max_users").notNull().default(5),
  features: text("features", { mode: "json" }).notNull().$type<Record<string, boolean>>(),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull(),
});

export const tenants = sqliteTable("tenants", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  name: text("name").notNull(),
  slug: text("slug").unique().notNull(),
  dbUrl: text("db_url").notNull(),
  dbTokenEncrypted: text("db_token_encrypted").notNull(),
  dbName: text("db_name"),
  tokenIssuedAt: integer("token_issued_at"),
  planId: text("plan_id").notNull().references(() => plans.id),
  status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),
  settings: text("settings", { mode: "json" }).$type<Record<string, unknown>>(),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull(),
  updatedAt: integer("updated_at").notNull(),
});

export const onboardingLocks = sqliteTable("onboarding_locks", {
  userId: text("user_id").primaryKey(),
  lockedAt: integer("locked_at").notNull(),
});

export const tenantInvitations = sqliteTable("tenant_invitations", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  tenantId: text("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  email: text("email").notNull(),
  role: text("role").notNull(),
  invitedBy: text("invited_by"),
  token: text("token"),
  expiresAt: integer("expires_at"),
  status: text("status").notNull().default("pending"),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull(),
});

export const globalUsers = sqliteTable("global_users", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  email: text("email").unique().notNull(),
  emailVerified: integer("email_verified"),
  verificationToken: text("verification_token"),
  verificationExpires: integer("verification_expires"),
  passwordResetToken: text("password_reset_token"),
  passwordResetExpires: integer("password_reset_expires"),
  phone: text("phone"),
  passwordHash: text("password_hash"),
  name: text("name"),
  avatarUrl: text("avatar_url"),
  sessionVersion: integer("session_version").default(1),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull(),
});

export const tenantMemberships = sqliteTable("tenant_memberships", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  userId: text("user_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => globalUsers.id),
  tenantId: text("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  role: text("role").notNull(),
  branchId: text("branch_id"),
  isActive: integer("is_active", { mode: "boolean" }).default(true),
  invitedBy: text("invited_by"),
  joinedAt: integer("joined_at").notNull(),
});

export const subscriptions = sqliteTable("subscriptions", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  tenantId: text("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  stripeCustomerId: text("stripe_customer_id"),
  stripeSubscriptionId: text("stripe_subscription_id"),
  status: text("status").notNull(),
  currentPeriodStart: integer("current_period_start"),
  currentPeriodEnd: integer("current_period_end"),
  cancelAtPeriodEnd: integer("cancel_at_period_end", { mode: "boolean" }).default(false),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull(),
});

});

export const notificationQueue = sqliteTable("notification_queue", {

input.prompt:
You are doing an exhaustive line-by-line code audit of the platform layer of the ADDPlus+ web app at /home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web. In July 2026 the web app was rebuilt into a multi-tenant SaaS ("Solera stack"): NextAuth v5 beta credentials auth against a metadata Turso DB via Drizzle, per-tenant Turso DBs with encrypted tokens, billing plans via PayHero, invitations, branches, Stream Chat messaging, web-push notifications, service worker + offline support.

Scope — read EVERY file in these areas completely:
- src/db/** (client.ts, schema/metadata.ts, schema/index.ts)
- src/lib/actions/** (all server actions: auth.ts, auth-email.ts, billing.ts, branch.ts, context.ts, invite.ts, messages.ts, notifications.ts, platform-support.ts, platform.ts, profile.ts, settings.ts)
- src/lib/auth.ts, session.ts, session-client.ts, rbac.ts, rbac-routes.ts, platform-admin.ts, membership.ts, tenant.ts, tenant-access.ts, require-writable-tenant (lib/api/), public-routes.ts, rate-limit.ts, crypto.ts, env.ts, auth-errors.ts, auth-urls.ts, invitations.ts, plans.ts, billing/payhero.ts, payhero-webhook.ts, payhero.ts, payments/** (confirm-sale.ts, payhero-status.ts, reference.ts, status.ts), mpesa.ts, email.ts, email-worker.ts, logger.ts, audit.ts, app-notifications.ts, app-shell-session.ts, notification-store.ts, theme-store.ts, toast.ts, utils.ts, validators.ts, api.ts, api-errors.ts, turso-api.ts, marketing-content.ts
- src/lib/messages/** (data, membership, platform-sync, presence, push, receipts, receipt-status, search, snapshot, types)
- src/lib/offline/** (cache, run-action, state, store), src/lib/stream/** (config, server), src/lib/sync/** (idempotency, permissions, replay)

1. SECURITY: server actions lacking auth checks (any user can call another tenant's action?), tenant isolation failures (queries not scoped by tenantId, cross-tenant data leaks), invite token generation/validation weaknesses (predictable tokens? no expiry enforcement?), password reset token handling, email verification bypass, rate limiting gaps on server actions, webhook secret verification on payhero callback, push subscription abuse.

3. Billing/plans: can users self-upgrade free? trial expiry enforcement actually enforced server-side anywhere besides middleware redirect?
4. NextAuth v5 beta pitfalls: JWT callback DB hits on every request (perf), sessionVersion invalidation logic errors.
5. Stream Chat: token endpoint auth, can a user get tokens for other users, API key exposure.
6. Service worker + offline replay: cache poisoning, stale auth, idempotency key handling.
7. Dead code / unused deps (e.g. react-query mounted but unused, duplicate toast libs react-hot-toast AND sonner, both @heroicons and lucide).
8. Env var mismatches vs .env.example, vercel.json, render.yaml at repo root, and next.config.js rewrites.
9. Any hardcoded emails, URLs, secrets, demo data left in production paths.
10. TypeScript type holes masked by ignoreBuildErrors — look for obviously wrong types/logic.

Report format: numbered findings each with SEVERITY (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), exact file path + line numbers, one-line description, brief evidence. End with a list of dead/duplicated dependencies and unused exports you found. Do not modify files.

WEB pages — fetch HTTP status + key content for at least: /, /marketplace, /vendors, /cart, /wishlist, /compare, /login, /signup, /verify-email, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /accept-invite, /pricing, /how-it-works, /faq, /about, /contact, /privacy, /terms, /status, /suspended, /trial-expired, /onboarding, /dashboard, /admin, /account, /products/new, /vendor/register, /flash-sales, /orders/abc123/track, /nonexistent-page-404-test. But note: failOrderPayment has NO checkoutRequestId match check — any 'failed' callback for an order reference cancels the order even if already confirmed? It updates status to cancelled unconditionally (even if confirmed!). Actually wait: if outcome==='failed', it goes straight to failOrderPayment which does `update where id` → sets cancelled regardless of current status. A replayed/duplicated failed callback after successful payment could cancel a PAID order. Race: confirm then duplicate failed → cancelled but money taken. That's a real bug (M/H severity).

authService.ts analysis — quite solid now, but findings:

1. **`/v1/auth/password/setup` has NO rate limit beyond global authLimiter (5/15min)** and no authentication: anyone who knows a phone number of an admin/vendor account WITHOUT a password can SET the password and take over the account! Flow: seeded admin exists without password_hash → attacker calls POST /v1/auth/password/setup {phone: 254115594826, password: 'attacker123'} → becomes admin. The only protection is that it requires password_hash to be null. In production, if Ken already set up his password, this is moot for that account. But ANY vendor account created via seed without password (or any future seeded accounts) is takeable by anyone who knows/guesses the phone. Also `registerAccount` creates customers with password; vendors register with password too now. So exposure is limited but real for pre-password seeded accounts. Severity HIGH (account takeover vector if any passwordless admin/vendor exists).

2. **User enumeration**: `loginWithPassword` returns `needsPasswordSetup: true` revealing that a phone belongs to an admin/vendor account without password. Combined with #1 — an attacker can enumerate phones and detect passwordless admin/vendor accounts, then set passwords. That's a takeover chain.

3. **verifyEmail token lookup**: token lookup doesn't compare timing-safe, fine at DB level. Code path with 6-digit code + email — brute-forceable? authLimiter 5 attempts/15min on /auth applies (skipSuccessfulRequests). 6-digit code = 1M combos; 5 tries per 15 min = 480/day... impractical. OK.

4. **resetPassword**: deletes refresh tokens — good. Doesn't bump sessionVersion (API JWTs are stateless 15m anyway).

5. **refreshToken rotation**: deletes old then issues new — good. But no reuse detection (if a stolen refresh token was already rotated, the thief's attempt just fails silently — fine).

6. **registerAccount email/phone binding logic**: if email taken AND same phone → proceeds to "existing" branch (phone exists check) → if existing.password_hash → 409 phone registered... wait: emailTaken && emailTaken.phone !== cleanPhone → 409. If emailTaken.phone === cleanPhone, falls through to existing lookup → existing found (same user) → if existing.password_hash set → throw 'Phone already registered'. Hmm — so a user re-registering with same email+phone gets 409 even though it's their own account. Minor UX. Not security.

7. **normalizePhone edge cases**: '+2547...' → strip '+' → starts with '254' ok. '07..' → '254' + rest. '7..' (9 digits after normalize?) — loginWithPassword uses normalizePhone which prepends 254 to anything not starting with 254 — e.g. identifier 'admin' → '254admin' → findUnique phone → null → invalid credentials. OK harmless.

8. **OTP paths disabled in prod** (ENABLE_OTP_AUTH=false on render.yaml) → 503. Good.

9. **generateReferralCode** collision possible (name+4 digits); referral_code unique constraint? Schema check needed. On collision → Prisma error → vendor registration fails randomly. Check schema for @unique on referral_code.

10. buildAuthResponse leaks needs_password_setup only for admin/vendor — fine.

11. **No login rate-limit per-account** (only IP-based authLimiter with skipSuccessfulRequests). Distributed brute force possible. Medium.

12. requestPasswordReset generic response — good anti-enumeration. BUT `emailSent: result.ok` returned in response — reveals whether email sent? Only when user exists. Actually `{...generic, emailSent}` only returned when user exists — so response shape differs (emailSent present vs absent) → enumeration via response field! Attacker: forgot-password for victim@x.com → response contains emailSent → account exists. MEDIUM info leak.

Wait — careful: `if (!user?.password_hash) return generic;` — no emailSent. Else returns {...generic, emailSent: result.ok}. So yes, presence of emailSent field = account exists with password. Enumeration confirmed (needs email format valid).

4	const deltaForType = (type: string, quantity: number): number => {
5	  switch (type) {

7	    case 'returned':
8	      return quantity
9	    case 'quantity_removed':
10	    case 'sold':
11	      return -quantity
12	    case 'adjustment':

21	    productId: string
22	    type: string
23	    quantity: number
24	    actorId?: string
25	    orderId?: string
26	    notes?: string
27	  }) {
28	    if (params.quantity <= 0) throw new AppError('Quantity must be positive', 400)
29	
30	    const delta = deltaForType(params.type, params.quantity)
31	
32	    return prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
33	      const product = await tx.product.findUnique({ where: { id: params.productId } })
34	      if (!product) throw new AppError('Product not found', 404)
35	
36	      const nextQty = product.stock_qty + delta
37	      if (nextQty < 0) throw new AppError('Insufficient stock', 400)
38	
39	      const movement = await tx.inventoryMovement.create({

44	          actor_id: params.actorId,

49	
50	      await tx.product.update({

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = ["driverAdapters"]
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = "file:./prisma/dev.db"
}

model User {
  id           String     @id @default(uuid())
  phone        String     @unique
  email        String?    @unique
  full_name    String?
  role          String
  status        String     @default("active")
  password_hash String?
  otp_verified  Boolean    @default(false)
  email_verified_at DateTime?
  email_verification_token String?
  email_verification_code String?
  email_verification_expires DateTime?
  password_reset_token String?
  password_reset_expires DateTime?
  push_token   String?
  created_at   DateTime   @default(now())
  updated_at   DateTime   @updatedAt
  deleted_at   DateTime?

  vendor_profile    VendorProfile?
  orders            Order[]
  disputes_opened   Dispute[]       @relation("dispute_opener")
  disputes_resolved Dispute[]       @relation("dispute_resolver")
  market_insights   MarketInsight[]
  refresh_tokens    RefreshToken[]

  @@map("users")
}

model VendorProfile {
  id                    String    @id @default(uuid())
  user_id               String    @unique
  business_name         String
  description           String?
  category_ids          String    @default("[]")
  location_lat          Float?
  location_lng          Float?
  location_address      String?
  mpesa_number          String
  kyc_status            String    @default("pending")
  compliance_score      Float     @default(0)
  is_suspended          Boolean   @default(false)
  fine_balance_cents    Int       @default(0)
  posting_ban_until     DateTime?
  business_photos       String    @default("[]")
  documents             String?
  partnership_signed_at DateTime?
  referral_code         String    @unique
  created_at            DateTime  @default(now())
  updated_at            DateTime  @updatedAt
  deleted_at            DateTime?

  user                 User                  @relation(fields: [user_id], references: [id])
  products             Product[]
  order_items          OrderItem[]
  escrow_entries       EscrowLedger[]
  fund_entries         CollectiveFund[]
  grants               GrantApplication[]
  compliance_logs      ComplianceLog[]
  posts                VendorPost[]
  referral_shares      ReferralShare[]
  importation_requests ImportationRequest[]

  @@map("vendor_profiles")
}

model Category {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  name        String   @unique
  slug        String   @unique
  parent_id   String?
  description String?
  icon        String?
  sort_order  Int      @default(0)
  is_active   Boolean  @default(true)
  created_at  DateTime @default(now())
  updated_at  DateTime @updatedAt

  parent   Category?  @relation("CategoryHierarchy", fields: [parent_id], references: [id])
  children Category[] @relation("CategoryHierarchy")
  products Product[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Product {
  id               String        @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id        String
  title            String
  description      String
  price_cents      Int
  compare_price_cents Int?
  category_id      String
  images           String        @default("[]")
  variants         String?
  stock_qty        Int           @default(0)
  status           String        @default("DRAFT")
  rejection_reason String?
  reviewed_at      DateTime?
  reviewed_by      String?
  submitted_at     DateTime?
  is_featured      Boolean       @default(false)
  importation_flag Boolean       @default(false)
  min_order_qty    Int           @default(1)
  views_count      Int           @default(0)
  sales_count      Int           @default(0)
  created_at       DateTime      @default(now())
  updated_at       DateTime      @updatedAt
  deleted_at       DateTime?

  vendor            VendorProfile      @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])
  category          Category           @relation(fields: [category_id], references: [id])
  order_items       OrderItem[]
  posts             VendorPost[]
  reviews           Review[]
  inventory_movements InventoryMovement[]

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([category_id])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("products")
}

model InventoryMovement {
  id         String                @id @default(uuid())
  product_id String
  type       String
  quantity   Int
  notes      String?
  actor_id   String?
  order_id   String?
  created_at DateTime              @default(now())

  product Product @relation(fields: [product_id], references: [id])

  @@index([product_id])
  @@index([created_at])
  @@map("inventory_movements")
}

model Review {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  product_id  String
  customer_id String
  order_id    String
  rating      Int
  comment     String?
  is_verified Boolean  @default(false)
  created_at  DateTime @default(now())
  updated_at  DateTime @updatedAt

  product Product @relation(fields: [product_id], references: [id])

  @@map("reviews")
}

model Order {
  id                  String      @id @default(uuid())
  customer_id         String
  status              String      @default("pending_payment")
  total_amount_cents  Int
  mpesa_ref           String?
  mpesa_request_id    String?
  mpesa_phone         String?
  delivery_address    String?
  delivery_notes      String?
  created_at          DateTime    @default(now())
  updated_at          DateTime    @updatedAt
  deleted_at          DateTime?

  customer    User        @relation(fields: [customer_id], references: [id])
  order_items OrderItem[]

  @@index([customer_id])
  @@index([status])
  @@index([mpesa_request_id])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id                    String       @id @default(uuid())
  order_id              String
  product_id            String
  vendor_id             String
  qty                   Int
  unit_price_cents      Int
  subtotal_cents        Int
  vendor_escrow_status  String       @default("held")
  item_status           String       @default("confirmed")
  delivery_confirmed_at DateTime?
  expected_delivery_at  DateTime?
  auto_release_at       DateTime?
  customer_notes        String?
  created_at            DateTime     @default(now())
  updated_at            DateTime     @updatedAt

  order        Order          @relation(fields: [order_id], references: [id])
  product      Product        @relation(fields: [product_id], references: [id])
  vendor       VendorProfile  @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])
  escrow_entry EscrowLedger?
  dispute      Dispute?

  @@index([order_id])
  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@map("order_items")
}

model EscrowLedger {
  id                          String       @id @default(uuid())
  order_item_id               String       @unique
  vendor_id                   String
  gross_amount_cents          Int
  levy_5pct_fund_cents        Int
  levy_5pct_profit_share_cents Int
  net_amount_cents            Int
  status                      String       @default("held")
  released_at                 DateTime?
  fine_deduction_cents        Int          @default(0)
  payout_mpesa_ref            String?
  created_at                  DateTime     @default(now())
  updated_at                  DateTime     @updatedAt

  order_item OrderItem     @relation(fields: [order_item_id], references: [id])
  vendor     VendorProfile @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("escrow_ledger")
}

model CollectiveFund {
  id                   String              @id @default(uuid())
  source_order_item_id String?
  vendor_id            String?
  amount_cents         Int
  type                 String
  notes                String?
  grant_id             String?
  created_at           DateTime            @default(now())

  vendor VendorProfile? @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([type])
  @@map("collective_fund")
}

model ComplianceLog {
  id                     String   @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id              String
  log_date               DateTime
  posts_made             Int      @default(0)
  posts_required         Int      @default(5)
  referrals_shared       Int      @default(0)
  referrals_required     Int      @default(3)
  profile_post_made      Boolean  @default(false)
  score                  Float    @default(0)
  fine_issued_amount_cents Int    @default(0)
  created_at             DateTime @default(now())

  vendor VendorProfile @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])

  @@unique([vendor_id, log_date])
  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([log_date])
  @@map("compliance_logs")
}

model VendorPost {
  id               String             @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id        String
  post_type        String
  product_id       String?
  caption          String
  images           String             @default("[]")
  platform_visible Boolean            @default(true)
  created_at       DateTime           @default(now())

  vendor  VendorProfile @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])
  product Product?      @relation(fields: [product_id], references: [id])

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([created_at])
  @@map("vendor_posts")
}

model ReferralShare {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id       String
  shared_at       DateTime @default(now())
  platform        String?
  screenshot_url  String?
  verified        Boolean  @default(false)
  week_start_date DateTime
  created_at      DateTime @default(now())

  vendor VendorProfile @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([week_start_date])
  @@map("referral_shares")
}

model ImportationRequest {
  id                          String            @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id                   String
  product_description         String
  target_qty                  Int
  max_price_cents             Int
  reference_image_url         String?
  cycle_month                 String
  status                      String            @default("submitted")
  deposit_amount_cents        Int?
  deposit_mpesa_ref           String?
  deposit_checkout_request_id String?
  admin_notes                 String?
  created_at                  DateTime          @default(now())
  updated_at                  DateTime          @updatedAt

  vendor VendorProfile @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([cycle_month])
  @@map("importation_requests")
}

model Dispute {
  id                 String        @id @default(uuid())
  order_item_id      String        @unique
  opened_by          String
  reason             String
  details            String?
  status             String        @default("open")
  resolution_notes   String?
  resolved_by        String?
  resolved_at        DateTime?
  refund_amount_cents Int?
  created_at         DateTime      @default(now())
  updated_at         DateTime      @updatedAt

  order_item OrderItem @relation(fields: [order_item_id], references: [id])
  opener     User      @relation("dispute_opener", fields: [opened_by], references: [id])
  resolver   User?     @relation("dispute_resolver", fields: [resolved_by], references: [id])

  @@index([status])
  @@map("disputes")
}

model GrantApplication {
  id                     String      @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id              String
  cycle_month            String
  business_plan_text     String
  requested_amount_cents Int?
  status                 String      @default("submitted")
  amount_approved_cents  Int?
  disbursement_mpesa_ref String?
  equity_stake_pct       Float?
  admin_notes            String?
  created_at             DateTime    @default(now())
  updated_at             DateTime    @updatedAt

  vendor VendorProfile @relation(fields: [vendor_id], references: [id])

  @@unique([vendor_id, cycle_month])
  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("grant_applications")
}

model MarketInsight {
  id           String    @id @default(uuid())
  author_id    String
  title        String
  body         String
  attachments  String?
  published_at DateTime?
  scheduled_at DateTime?
  is_published Boolean   @default(false)
  created_at   DateTime  @default(now())
  updated_at   DateTime  @updatedAt

  author User @relation(fields: [author_id], references: [id])

  @@index([is_published])
  @@index([published_at])
  @@map("market_insights")
}

model OtpCode {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  phone      String
  code       String
  expires_at DateTime
  used       Boolean  @default(false)
  created_at DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([phone, used])
  @@map("otp_codes")
}

model RefreshToken {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  user_id    String
  token      String   @unique
  expires_at DateTime
  created_at DateTime @default(now())

  user User @relation(fields: [user_id], references: [id])

  @@index([user_id])
  @@index([token])
  @@map("refresh_tokens")
}

model FineLedger {
  id                   String    @id @default(uuid())
  vendor_id            String
  amount_cents         Int
  reason               String
  rule_violated        String
  strike_level         Int       @default(1)
  issued_by            String?
  is_paid              Boolean   @default(false)
  paid_at              DateTime?
  deducted_from_escrow Boolean   @default(false)
  created_at           DateTime  @default(now())
  updated_at           DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([vendor_id])
  @@index([is_paid])
  @@map("fine_ledger")
}

model Setting {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  key         String   @unique
  value       String
  description String?
  updated_at  DateTime @updatedAt
  updated_by  String?

  @@map("settings")
}

model ActivityLog {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  actor_id    String
  actor_role  String
  action      String
  entity_type String
  entity_id   String
  metadata    String?
  ip_address  String?
  created_at  DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([actor_id])
  @@index([entity_type, entity_id])
  @@index([action])
  @@index([created_at])
  @@map("activity_logs")
}

# Security Audit & Fixes - ADDPlus+

**Date:** May 2026
**Auditor:** Vibe Security Assessment

---

## Identified Vulnerabilities

### 1. Insecure Token Storage (HIGH)
**Location:** `apps/web/src/lib/api.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/login/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/vendor/register/page.tsx`

**Issue:** JWT access and refresh tokens are stored in `localStorage`, making them vulnerable to:
- XSS attacks (malicious scripts can access localStorage)
- Session hijacking via JavaScript injection

**Fix Applied:**
- Added `httpOnly` cookie support in API interceptor
- Created secure storage utility with encryption
- Tokens now use cryptographically secure random generation

### 2. Predictable Token Generation (MEDIUM)
**Location:** Multiple auth pages using `demo-token-${Date.now()}`

**Issue:** Using `Date.now()` for token generation is predictable and can be exploited.

**Fix Applied:**
- Implemented `crypto.randomUUID()` for secure token generation
- Added fallback for older browsers using `Math.random()` with entropy mixing

...

38	- **Auth.js v5 beta** — credentials-only, bcrypt cost 12, JWT 24h maxAge, `session_version` invalidation
39	- **PayHero Kenya** — M-Pesa STK at `https://backend.payhero.co.ke/api/v2/payments`; Daraja `/api/mpesa/callback` returns **501**
40	- **Brevo** — transactional email; optional Conversations widget

42	- **Messaging** — SSE (`/api/messages/stream`), presence, typing, read receipts, platform support escalation

51	     → requireAppSession(module) | requireTenantAction(module, action)
52	     → getTenantContext() → decrypt db token → tenant Drizzle client
53	     → resolveBranchId() → Zod → Drizzle write → auditLog() (metadata)
54	```
55	
56	**Tenant lifecycle:** signup → email verify → `/onboarding` → `pending_approval` (demo/read-only) → platform admin approves → **14-day trial** → PayHero subscribe → `active`. Also: `trial_expired`, `suspended`.
57	
58	**Access modes** (`lib/tenant-access.ts`): `demo` | `trial` | `full` | `blocked`
59

63	
64	`plans`, `tenants`, `onboarding_locks`, `tenant_invitations`, `global_users`, `tenant_memberships`, `subscriptions`, `audit_logs`, `notification_queue`, `compliance_requests`, `profile_change_requests`, `platform_support_tickets`, `platform_support_messages`, `push_subscriptions`
65	
66	CaspaHub adds: `consumer_booking_index` (cross-tenant booking lookup).
67	
68	Runtime-created (not in Drizzle): `rate_limits`, per-tenant `sync_logs`.

70	## Where to edit what (shared paths)
71	
72	| Concern | Path |
73	|---------|------|
74	| Tenant provision | `lib/tenant.ts` — DB names: `solera-{slug}-*`, `edifice-{slug}-*`, `caspahub-{slug}-*` |
75	| RBAC matrix | `lib/rbac.ts` |
76	| Route → module map | `lib/rbac-routes.ts` |
77	| Session guards | `lib/session.ts`, `lib/actions/context.ts` |
78	| Billing | `lib/billing/payhero.ts`, `lib/actions/billing.ts` |
79	| PayHero STK | `lib/payhero.ts`, `lib/payhero-webhook.ts` |
80	| Messaging | `lib/messages/*`, `lib/actions/messages.ts` |
81	| Marketing copy | `lib/marketing-content.ts` |
82	| Middleware | `src/middleware.ts` |
83	| Offline | `lib/offline/*`, `lib/sync/replay.ts`, `POST /api/sync` |
84	| Env validation | `lib/env.ts` |
85	
86	## Solera — pharmacy & clinic SaaS
87	
88	**Tagline:** Pharmacy/clinic management for Kenya/Africa.
89	
90	**9 app modules:** dashboard, inventory, pos, prescriptions, patients, clinic, reports, messages, settings
91	
92	**7 roles:** super_admin, admin, pharmacist, cashier, doctor, nurse, receptionist
93	
94	**Domain actions:** `lib/actions/pharmacy.ts` (inventory, POS, patients, Rx), `lib/actions/clinic.ts` (appointments, consultations, vitals)
95	
96	**Key tenant tables:** `products`, `inventory_batches`, `patients`, `prescriptions`, `sales`, `shifts`, `appointments`, `consultations`, `vitals`
97	
98	**Unique strengths:**
99	- PHI encryption active (`lib/phi.ts` — 11 patient fields with `enc:` prefix)
100	- Offline sync **working** — replays sales, patients, Rx, inventory, clinic ops
101	- POS with FIFO batch deduction, M-Pesa STK at checkout, barcode scanning
102	- Rx → POS deep link (`?prescriptionId=`)
103	- Kenya regulatory stubs: PPB, ODPC, NHIF, KRA (`lib/compliance/`)
104	
105	**Plan gate:** `hasClinic` on Professional plan.
106	
107	## Edifice — school operating system
108	
109	**Tagline:** "Every School. One Brain."
110	
111	**25 app modules:** dashboard, students, admissions, academic, attendance, gradebook, lms, timetable, finance, hr, library, transport, hostel, communications, portal, health, events, inventory, alumni, ai-insights, analytics, reports, messages, settings, account
112	
113	**7 roles:** super_admin, admin, teacher, parent, finance_officer, nurse, receptionist
114	
115	**Domain actions:** `lib/actions/school.ts` (~30 CRUD actions)
116	
117	**Key tenant tables:** `students`, `parent_student_links`, `staff_members`, `classes`, `subjects`, `attendance_records`, `grade_distributions`, `fee_records`, `admissions`, `health_records`, `transport_routes`, `hostel_rooms`, etc. (29 tables)

120	- Parent portal (`/portal`) — parents see only linked children via `parent_student_links`
121	- Parent invites carry `linkedStudentId` on `tenant_invitations`
122	- Timetable auto-generate (`generateTimetable`)
123	- AI insights (`/ai-insights`) — rule-based heuristics (at-risk students, fee defaulters), not ML
124	- Module UI pattern: `ModuleKpiGrid`, `ModuleDataPanel`, `ModuleQuickLinks` (`lib/modules/quick-links.ts`)
125	- Parallel DDL in `lib/tenant-schema.ts` + Drizzle `tenant.ts`
126	
127	**Plan gate:** `hasMultiCampus` (Professional — hostel/transport).
128	
129	**Gaps:** Offline replay **stub** (always throws). No per-student M-Pesa fees. No pagination. School fees via M-Pesa not wired.
130	
131	**Ghost code from Solera port:** `pos-client.tsx` (no `/pos` route), `phi.ts` (zero callers), `barcode.ts`, `confirmSalePayment()` stub, `assertClinicModuleAllowed()` repurposed.
132	
133	## CaspaHub — car wash booking OS
134	
135	**Tagline:** "East Africa's car wash platform — start with bookings, grow into the full OS."
136	
137	**13 operator modules:** dashboard, bookings, queue, customers, staff, payments, loyalty, analytics, fleet, reports, settings, messages
138	
139	**6 operator roles + consumer:** super_admin, admin, manager, supervisor, attendant, cashier, consumer
140	
141	**Domain actions:** `lib/actions/wash.ts` (queue, walk-ins, services, CRM)
142	
143	**Key tenant tables (car wash):** `wash_services`, `wash_bookings`, `wash_booking_events`
144	
145	**Consumer routes (public):** `/find` → `/book/[branchId]` → STK pay → `/track/[bookingId]`
146	
147	**Booking status machine:** `BOOKED → QUEUED → BAY_ASSIGNED → WASHING → READY → COMPLETED` (+ `CANCELLED`)
148

150	
151	**Unique features:**
152	- Consumer booking flow with rate-limited public API
153	- Live queue board (`/queue`) with Advance / Mark Ready
154	- Fleet = vehicles with ≥3 visits (query on `wash_bookings`, no dedicated table)
155	- Loyalty UI from booking aggregates; `recordLoyaltyTransaction()` is a **stub**
156	
157	**Plan pricing:** Starter free (booking), Professional KES 4,999/mo (CRM, fleet, analytics).
158	
159	**Critical:** README is **stale** — describes Prisma + three Vercel surfaces (`CASPAHUB_SURFACE`). **Source code is SSOT.** Now unified Drizzle platform like Solera.
160	
161	**Ghost code:** Full pharmacy schema + `lib/actions/pharmacy.ts` and `lib/actions/carwash.ts` (identical ~890 LOC pharmacy POS code). `phi.ts`, `compliance/*`, `barcode.ts` unused.
162	
163	## API routes (shared across all three)
164	
165	| Route | Purpose |
166	|-------|---------|
167	| `/api/auth/[...nextauth]` | Auth.js handlers |
168	| `/api/health` | Metadata DB liveness |
169	| `/api/payhero/callback` | PayHero webhook (subscriptions + sales) |
170	| `/api/mpesa/callback` | 501 — Daraja not configured |
171	| `/api/payments/status` | Poll STK payment outcome |
172	| `/api/sync` | Offline operation replay |
173	| `/api/admin/tenants` | Platform admin tenant list |
174	| `/api/messages/stream` | SSE messaging |
175	| `/api/messages/poll` | Message polling fallback |
176	| `/api/messages/presence` | Staff heartbeat |
177	| `/api/messages/typing` | Typing indicators |
178	| `/api/messages/search` | Message search |
179	| `/api/messages/push` | Web Push subscribe |
180	
181	**CaspaHub-only:** `/api/branches`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings/[id]/track`, `/api/payments/mpesa/stk-push`
182	
183	## GetStream Chat (Stream Chat) integration
184	
185	Use this section when adding Stream Chat to any of the four desktop projects. It is written to map your current messaging stack (SSE, poll, presence, typing, receipts, tickets) to Stream Chat without guessing.
186	
187	### Purpose by project
188	
189	- **Solera** (`~/Desktop/solera`): staff team communication and ticket-based support in `/messages` (currently `MessagesClient` + `PushPrompt`).
190	- **Edifice** (`~/Desktop/edifice`): staff communication and school support workflows in `/messages` (same pattern as Solera).
191	- **CaspaHub** (`~/Desktop/caspahub`): operator coordination and support workflows in `/messages` (same pattern as Solera).
192	- **ADDPlus+** (`~/Desktop/addplus`): `/messages` is currently a placeholder page ("In-app messaging is coming soon"), so Stream Chat should be treated as the first full in-app messaging rollout for this product.
193	
194	### Domain mapping: current model -> Stream primitives
195	
196	| Current model | Stream Chat equivalent | Notes |
197	|---|---|---|
198	| `conversations` (`direct` / `group` / `ticket`) | Channel (`messaging` type, custom fields for subtype) | Keep conversation subtype in channel custom data for UI filtering. |
199	| `conversation_members` | Channel members | Sync on create/update to keep Stream membership authoritative. |
200	| `messages` (`text` / `image` / `system`) | Stream messages + attachments | Map `system` to Stream system-style rendering or message custom field. |
201	| `typing_indicators` | Typing events | Stream UI handles this automatically; custom UIs use `keystroke()` and `stopTyping()`. |
202	| `staff_presence` | Presence events | Watch channels with presence enabled and listen to `user.presence.changed`. |
203	| `message_deliveries` + `lastReadAt` logic | Read events + unread counts | Use Stream `markRead` and channel unread state. |
204	| `messages/search.ts` | Stream search API | Use channel filters + query/message filters for scoped search. |
205	
206	### Recommended migration strategy
207	
208	Default recommendation is **incremental hybrid migration**:
209	
210	1. Keep existing conversation and ticket records for business workflows and auditability.
211	2. Move real-time transport and message delivery UX to Stream Chat.
212	3. Replace only the message thread/composer surface first; keep your current sidebar/ticket domain UI.
213	4. Retire SSE/poll endpoints only after parity verification.
214	
215	### Staged implementation workflow
216	
217	- **Stage 0 - configuration**
218	  - Add `STREAM_API_KEY`, `STREAM_API_SECRET` (server only), and any per-app/public key wiring needed for web/mobile clients.
219	  - Add Stream server/client SDK packages in each repo that will host chat.
220	- **Stage 1 - auth/token endpoint**
221	  - Create a server endpoint that validates your app session and returns `createToken(userId)` from a server-side Stream client.
222	  - User ID passed to Stream must be stable across sessions and tenants.
223	- **Stage 2 - channel bootstrapping and membership sync**
224	  - On direct/group/ticket conversation creation, create/update corresponding Stream channel.
225	  - Keep a deterministic mapping key (for example, a channel id derived from your `conversationId`).
226	  - Sync members whenever conversation membership changes.
227	- **Stage 3 - UI and realtime cutover**
228	  - Replace SSE (`/api/messages/stream`) and poll (`/api/messages/poll`) in active message threads with Stream channel state/events.
229	  - Migrate typing, unread/read receipts, and presence UI to Stream-provided state.
230	- **Stage 4 - ticket escalation parity**
231	  - Keep platform escalation logic in your DB/service layer.
232	  - Mirror important ticket state transitions into Stream messages/events for operator visibility.
233	
234	### UI integration options
235	
236	- **Recommended (hybrid):** keep existing conversation/ticket list UX and swap message thread + composer to Stream React UI components.
237	- **Alternative (adapter):** keep full custom `MessagesClient` UX and replace only data/transport with Stream APIs/events.
238	
239	### Exact code touchpoints to wire
240	
241	- **Solera/Edifice/CaspaHub**
242	  - API transport: `src/app/api/messages/*/route.ts`
243	  - Message mutations and workflow logic: `src/lib/actions/messages.ts`
244	  - Message data/read model: `src/lib/messages/*`
245	  - Message UI: `src/components/messages/*`
246	  - Message page entry: `src/app/(app)/messages/page.tsx`
247	- **ADDPlus+**
248	  - Placeholder entry page: `apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/page.tsx`
249	  - Existing messaging UI library: `apps/web/src/components/messages/*`
250	  - Existing messaging action layer: `apps/web/src/lib/actions/messages.ts`
251	  - Existing message data/read model: `apps/web/src/lib/messages/*`
252	
253	### Stream feature checklist for parity
254	
255	Enable or verify these capabilities in Stream channel type configuration before rollout:
256	
257	- typing events
258	- read events / unread counts
259	- message search
260	- file/image uploads
261	- replies/threads (if you use threaded support workflows)
262	- presence updates
263	
264	## Porting features between repos
265	
266	1. **Platform features** (auth, billing, messaging, admin, settings, offline infra) — usually identical; diff before copying.
267	2. **Domain features** — never copy `pharmacy.ts` ↔ `school.ts` ↔ `wash.ts` wholesale; adapt schema + RBAC module names.
268	3. **RBAC** — always update **both** `rbac.ts` and `rbac-routes.ts`.
269	4. **Schema** — tenant DDL via `migrateTenantSchema()` in `lib/tenant.ts` (runtime SQL); metadata via `scripts/migrate-metadata.ts`.
270	5. **Plans** — seed `starter` / `professional` in metadata; feature flags in `plans.features` JSON differ per product.
271	
272	## Commands (all three)
273	
274	```bash
275	npm install && cp .env.example .env.local   # Edifice: copy from Solera or migration-backup
276	npm run db:migrate                          # metadata schema + plan seed
277	npm run db:migrate-tenants                  # batch tenant migrations
278	npm run dev                                 # localhost:3000
279	npm test                                    # RBAC, PayHero, receipts, theme unit tests
280	npm run build && npm start                  # PWA (SW disabled in dev)
281	```
282	
283	**Required env:** `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`, `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TURSO_API_TOKEN`, `AUTH_SECRET`
284	
285	**Recommended:** `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS`, `PAYHERO_*`, `BREVO_API_KEY`
286	
287	## Production readiness snapshot
288	
289	| Area | Solera | Edifice | CaspaHub |
290	|------|--------|---------|----------|
291	| Core domain | ✅ Mature MVP | ⚠️ 25 modules, partial CRUD | ✅ Booking/queue core works |
292	| Offline/PWA | ✅ POS queue sync | ❌ Replay stub | ⚠️ Wash-specific sync |
293	| CI | ✅ lint + build + audit | ❌ No CI | ✅ tsc + test + build |
294	| Per-entity M-Pesa | ✅ POS sales | ❌ School fees not wired | ✅ Booking STK |
295	| Messaging | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full |
296	| Ghost code | Minimal | Pharmacy-era leftovers | Pharmacy schema + duplicate actions |
297	| `.env.example` | ✅ | ❌ (migration-backup only) | ✅ |
298	| SSOT README | ✅ Exhaustive | ✅ Exhaustive | ⚠️ Stale (Prisma era) |
299	
300	## ADDPlus+ relationship
301	
302	ADDPlus+ solves a **different problem** (multi-vendor marketplace with escrow) and shares only the author and Kenya market focus. Do **not** assume Drizzle/tenant-per-DB patterns apply when working in addplus.
303	
304	| ADDPlus+ unique | Vertical SaaS unique |
305	|-----------------|---------------------|
306	| Prisma + shared Turso | Drizzle + DB-per-tenant |
307	| Express API on Render | Server Actions in Next.js |
308	| Vendor/customer/admin roles | 7-role RBAC per vertical |
309	| Escrow + collective fund | SaaS subscription billing |
310	| Expo mobile app | Serwist PWA |
311	| Daraja M-Pesa (partial E2E) | PayHero M-Pesa (working) |
312	
313	## Do not trust
314	
315	- Solera `docs/GAPS.md` — stale; README is SSOT
316	- Edifice `.agents/memory/` and `.migration-backup/` — historical Scholr prototype
317	- CaspaHub `README.md` — describes Prisma/three-surface architecture; **code uses Drizzle unified platform**
318	- CaspaHub `.cursor/skills/solera-edifice-platform/SKILL.md` — says CaspaHub uses Prisma; **outdated**
319	- `subscriptions.stripe_*` columns — store PayHero refs, not Stripe
320	
321	## Additional reference
322	
323	For full route lists, schema tables, middleware rules, and file-by-file notes, see [reference.md](reference.md).

**Access modes** (`lib/tenant-access.ts`): `demo` | `trial` | `full` | `blocked`

**Plans** (metadata `plans` table): `starter` (KES 6,500/mo) and `professional` (KES 13,000/mo) — feature flags differ per product.

## Metadata DB tables (all three)

`plans`, `tenants`, `onboarding_locks`, `tenant_invitations`, `global_users`, `tenant_memberships`, `subscriptions`, `audit_logs`, `notification_queue`, `compliance_requests`, `profile_change_requests`, `platform_support_tickets`, `platform_support_messages`, `push_subscriptions`

CaspaHub adds: `consumer_booking_index` (cross-tenant booking lookup).

Runtime-created (not in Drizzle): `rate_limits`, per-tenant `sync_logs`.

## Where to edit what (shared paths)

| Concern | Path |
|---------|------|
| Tenant provision | `lib/tenant.ts` — DB names: `solera-{slug}-*`, `edifice-{slug}-*`, `caspahub-{slug}-*` |
| RBAC matrix | `lib/rbac.ts` |
| Route → module map | `lib/rbac-routes.ts` |
| Session guards | `lib/session.ts`, `lib/actions/context.ts` |
| Billing | `lib/billing/payhero.ts`, `lib/actions/billing.ts` |
| PayHero STK | `lib/payhero.ts`, `lib/payhero-webhook.ts` |
| Messaging | `lib/messages/*`, `lib/actions/messages.ts` |
| Marketing copy | `lib/marketing-content.ts` |
| Middleware | `src/middleware.ts` |
| Offline | `lib/offline/*`, `lib/sync/replay.ts`, `POST /api/sync` |
| Env validation | `lib/env.ts` |

## Solera — pharmacy & clinic SaaS

**Tagline:** Pharmacy/clinic management for Kenya/Africa.

**9 app modules:** dashboard, inventory, pos, prescriptions, patients, clinic, reports, messages, settings

**7 roles:** super_admin, admin, pharmacist, cashier, doctor, nurse, receptionist

**Domain actions:** `lib/actions/pharmacy.ts` (inventory, POS, patients, Rx), `lib/actions/clinic.ts` (appointments, consultations, vitals)

**Key tenant tables:** `products`, `inventory_batches`, `patients`, `prescriptions`, `sales`, `shifts`, `appointments`, `consultations`, `vitals`

**Unique strengths:**
- PHI encryption active (`lib/phi.ts` — 11 patient fields with `enc:` prefix)
- Offline sync **working** — replays sales, patients, Rx, inventory, clinic ops
- POS with FIFO batch deduction, M-Pesa STK at checkout, barcode scanning
- Rx → POS deep link (`?prescriptionId=`)
- Kenya regulatory stubs: PPB, ODPC, NHIF, KRA (`lib/compliance/`)

**Plan gate:** `hasClinic` on Professional plan.

## Edifice — school operating system

**Tagline:** "Every School. One Brain."

**25 app modules:** dashboard, students, admissions, academic, attendance, gradebook, lms, timetable, finance, hr, library, transport, hostel, communications, portal, health, events, inventory, alumni, ai-insights, analytics, reports, messages, settings, account

**7 roles:** super_admin, admin, teacher, parent, finance_officer, nurse, receptionist

**Domain actions:** `lib/actions/school.ts` (~30 CRUD actions)

**Key tenant tables:** `students`, `parent_student_links`, `staff_members`, `classes`, `subjects`, `attendance_records`, `grade_distributions`, `fee_records`, `admissions`, `health_records`, `transport_routes`, `hostel_rooms`, etc. (29 tables)

**Unique features:**
- Parent portal (`/portal`) — parents see only linked children via `parent_student_links`
- Parent invites carry `linkedStudentId` on `tenant_invitations`
- Timetable auto-generate (`generateTimetable`)
- AI insights (`/ai-insights`) — rule-based heuristics (at-risk students, fee defaulters), not ML
- Module UI pattern: `ModuleKpiGrid`, `ModuleDataPanel`, `ModuleQuickLinks` (`lib/modules/quick-links.ts`)
- Parallel DDL in `lib/tenant-schema.ts` + Drizzle `tenant.ts`

**Plan gate:** `hasMultiCampus` (Professional — hostel/transport).

**Gaps:** Offline replay **stub** (always throws). No per-student M-Pesa fees. No pagination. School fees via M-Pesa not wired.

**Ghost code from Solera port:** `pos-client.tsx` (no `/pos` route), `phi.ts` (zero callers), `barcode.ts`, `confirmSalePayment()` stub, `assertClinicModuleAllowed()` repurposed.

## CaspaHub — car wash booking OS

**Tagline:** "East Africa's car wash platform — start with bookings, grow into the full OS."

**13 operator modules:** dashboard, bookings, queue, customers, staff, payments, loyalty, analytics, fleet, reports, settings, messages

**6 operator roles + consumer:** super_admin, admin, manager, supervisor, attendant, cashier, consumer

**Domain actions:** `lib/actions/wash.ts` (queue, walk-ins, services, CRM)

**Key tenant tables (car wash):** `wash_services`, `wash_bookings`, `wash_booking_events`

**Consumer routes (public):** `/find` → `/book/[branchId]` → STK pay → `/track/[bookingId]`

**Booking status machine:** `BOOKED → QUEUED → BAY_ASSIGNED → WASHING → READY → COMPLETED` (+ `CANCELLED`)

**Cross-tenant bookings:** Branch IDs are `tenantId:branchId`; metadata `consumer_booking_index` maps booking → tenant; `/api/branches` aggregates across tenants.

**Unique features:**
- Consumer booking flow with rate-limited public API
- Live queue board (`/queue`) with Advance / Mark Ready
- Fleet = vehicles with ≥3 visits (query on `wash_bookings`, no dedicated table)
- Loyalty UI from booking aggregates; `recordLoyaltyTransaction()` is a **stub**

**Plan pricing:** Starter free (booking), Professional KES 4,999/mo (CRM, fleet, analytics).

**Critical:** README is **stale** — describes Prisma + three Vercel surfaces (`CASPAHUB_SURFACE`). **Source code is SSOT.** Now unified Drizzle platform like Solera.

**Ghost code:** Full pharmacy schema + `lib/actions/pharmacy.ts` and `lib/actions/carwash.ts` (identical ~890 LOC pharmacy POS code). `phi.ts`, `compliance/*`, `barcode.ts` unused.

## API routes (shared across all three)

| Route | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `/api/auth/[...nextauth]` | Auth.js handlers |
| `/api/health` | Metadata DB liveness |
| `/api/payhero/callback` | PayHero webhook (subscriptions + sales) |
| `/api/mpesa/callback` | 501 — Daraja not configured |
| `/api/payments/status` | Poll STK payment outcome |
| `/api/sync` | Offline operation replay |
| `/api/admin/tenants` | Platform admin tenant list |
| `/api/messages/stream` | SSE messaging |
| `/api/messages/poll` | Message polling fallback |
| `/api/messages/presence` | Staff heartbeat |
| `/api/messages/typing` | Typing indicators |
| `/api/messages/search` | Message search |
| `/api/messages/push` | Web Push subscribe |

**CaspaHub-only:** `/api/branches`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings/[id]/track`, `/api/payments/mpesa/stk-push`

## GetStream Chat (Stream Chat) integration

Use this section when adding Stream Chat to any of the four desktop projects. It is written to map your current messaging stack (SSE, poll, presence, typing, receipts, tickets) to Stream Chat without guessing.

### Purpose by project

- **Solera** (`~/Desktop/solera`): staff team communication and ticket-based support in `/messages` (currently `MessagesClient` + `PushPrompt`).
- **Edifice** (`~/Desktop/edifice`): staff communication and school support workflows in `/messages` (same pattern as Solera).
- **CaspaHub** (`~/Desktop/caspahub`): operator coordination and support workflows in `/messages` (same pattern as Solera).
- **ADDPlus+** (`~/Desktop/addplus`): `/messages` is currently a placeholder page ("In-app messaging is coming soon"), so Stream Chat should be treated as the first full in-app messaging rollout for this product.

### Domain mapping: current model -> Stream primitives

| Current model | Stream Chat equivalent | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `conversations` (`direct` / `group` / `ticket`) | Channel (`messaging` type, custom fields for subtype) | Keep conversation subtype in channel custom data for UI filtering. |
| `conversation_members` | Channel members | Sync on create/update to keep Stream membership authoritative. |
| `messages` (`text` / `image` / `system`) | Stream messages + attachments | Map `system` to Stream system-style rendering or message custom field. |
| `typing_indicators` | Typing events | Stream UI handles this automatically; custom UIs use `keystroke()` and `stopTyping()`. |
| `staff_presence` | Presence events | Watch channels with presence enabled and listen to `user.presence.changed`. |
| `message_deliveries` + `lastReadAt` logic | Read events + unread counts | Use Stream `markRead` and channel unread state. |
| `messages/search.ts` | Stream search API | Use channel filters + query/message filters for scoped search. |

### Recommended migration strategy

Default recommendation is **incremental hybrid migration**:

1. Keep existing conversation and ticket records for business workflows and auditability.
2. Move real-time transport and message delivery UX to Stream Chat.
3. Replace only the message thread/composer surface first; keep your current sidebar/ticket domain UI.
4. Retire SSE/poll endpoints only after parity verification.

### Staged implementation workflow

- **Stage 0 - configuration**
  - Add `STREAM_API_KEY`, `STREAM_API_SECRET` (server only), and any per-app/public key wiring needed for web/mobile clients.
  - Add Stream server/client SDK packages in each repo that will host chat.
- **Stage 1 - auth/token endpoint**
  - Create a server endpoint that validates your app session and returns `createToken(userId)` from a server-side Stream client.
  - User ID passed to Stream must be stable across sessions and tenants.
- **Stage 2 - channel bootstrapping and membership sync**
  - On direct/group/ticket conversation creation, create/update corresponding Stream channel.
  - Keep a deterministic mapping key (for example, a channel id derived from your `conversationId`).
  - Sync members whenever conversation membership changes.
- **Stage 3 - UI and realtime cutover**
  - Replace SSE (`/api/messages/stream`) and poll (`/api/messages/poll`) in active message threads with Stream channel state/events.
  - Migrate typing, unread/read receipts, and presence UI to Stream-provided state.
- **Stage 4 - ticket escalation parity**
  - Keep platform escalation logic in your DB/service layer.
  - Mirror important ticket state transitions into Stream messages/events for operator visibility.

### UI integration options

- **Recommended (hybrid):** keep existing conversation/ticket list UX and swap message thread + composer to Stream React UI components.
- **Alternative (adapter):** keep full custom `MessagesClient` UX and replace only data/transport with Stream APIs/events.

### Exact code touchpoints to wire

- **Solera/Edifice/CaspaHub**
  - API transport: `src/app/api/messages/*/route.ts`
  - Message mutations and workflow logic: `src/lib/actions/messages.ts`
  - Message data/read model: `src/lib/messages/*`
  - Message UI: `src/components/messages/*`
  - Message page entry: `src/app/(app)/messages/page.tsx`
- **ADDPlus+**
  - Placeholder entry page: `apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/page.tsx`
  - Existing messaging UI library: `apps/web/src/components/messages/*`
  - Existing messaging action layer: `apps/web/src/lib/actions/messages.ts`
  - Existing message data/read model: `apps/web/src/lib/messages/*`

### Stream feature checklist for parity

Enable or verify these capabilities in Stream channel type configuration before rollout:

- typing events
- read events / unread counts
- message search
- file/image uploads
- replies/threads (if you use threaded support workflows)
- presence updates

## Porting features between repos

1. **Platform features** (auth, billing, messaging, admin, settings, offline infra) — usually identical; diff before copying.
2. **Domain features** — never copy `pharmacy.ts` ↔ `school.ts` ↔ `wash.ts` wholesale; adapt schema + RBAC module names.
3. **RBAC** — always update **both** `rbac.ts` and `rbac-routes.ts`.
4. **Schema** — tenant DDL via `migrateTenantSchema()` in `lib/tenant.ts` (runtime SQL); metadata via `scripts/migrate-metadata.ts`.
5. **Plans** — seed `starter` / `professional` in metadata; feature flags in `plans.features` JSON differ per product.

## Commands (all three)

```bash
npm install && cp .env.example .env.local   # Edifice: copy from Solera or migration-backup
npm run db:migrate                          # metadata schema + plan seed
npm run db:migrate-tenants                  # batch tenant migrations
npm run dev                                 # localhost:3000
npm test                                    # RBAC, PayHero, receipts, theme unit tests
npm run build && npm start                  # PWA (SW disabled in dev)
```

**Required env:** `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`, `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TURSO_API_TOKEN`, `AUTH_SECRET`

**Recommended:** `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS`, `PAYHERO_*`, `BREVO_API_KEY`

## Production readiness snapshot

| Area | Solera | Edifice | CaspaHub |
|------|--------|---------|----------|
| Core domain | ✅ Mature MVP | ⚠️ 25 modules, partial CRUD | ✅ Booking/queue core works |
| Offline/PWA | ✅ POS queue sync | ❌ Replay stub | ⚠️ Wash-specific sync |
| CI | ✅ lint + build + audit | ❌ No CI | ✅ tsc + test + build |
| Per-entity M-Pesa | ✅ POS sales | ❌ School fees not wired | ✅ Booking STK |
| Messaging | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full |
| Ghost code | Minimal | Pharmacy-era leftovers | Pharmacy schema + duplicate actions |
| `.env.example` | ✅ | ❌ (migration-backup only) | ✅ |
| SSOT README | ✅ Exhaustive | ✅ Exhaustive | ⚠️ Stale (Prisma era) |

## ADDPlus+ relationship

ADDPlus+ solves a **different problem** (multi-vendor marketplace with escrow) and shares only the author and Kenya market focus. Do **not** assume Drizzle/tenant-per-DB patterns apply when working in addplus.

| ADDPlus+ unique | Vertical SaaS unique |
|-----------------|---------------------|
| Prisma + shared Turso | Drizzle + DB-per-tenant |
| Express API on Render | Server Actions in Next.js |
| Vendor/customer/admin roles | 7-role RBAC per vertical |
| Escrow + collective fund | SaaS subscription billing |
| Expo mobile app | Serwist PWA |
| Daraja M-Pesa (partial E2E) | PayHero M-Pesa (working) |

## Do not trust

- Solera `docs/GAPS.md` — stale; README is SSOT
- Edifice `.agents/memory/` and `.migration-backup/` — historical Scholr prototype
- CaspaHub `README.md` — describes Prisma/three-surface architecture; **code uses Drizzle unified platform**
- CaspaHub `.cursor/skills/solera-edifice-platform/SKILL.md` — says CaspaHub uses Prisma; **outdated**
- `subscriptions.stripe_*` columns — store PayHero refs, not Stripe

## Additional reference

For full route lists, schema tables, middleware rules, and file-by-file notes, see [reference.md](reference.md).

2	
3	This document is the **acceptance matrix** used to bring ADDPlus+ up to the same product-quality standard as **Solera**, **Edifice**, and **CaspaHub**.
4	
5	**Strict parity** means:

7	- ADDPlus+ must also meet **Edifice’s multi-module consistency** (module KPI/data panel/quick links primitives).
8	- ADDPlus+ must also meet **CaspaHub’s ops-first dashboard patterns** (events/ops paneling, action affordances).
9	
10	Where a benchmark feature is **domain-specific** (e.g., patients vs students vs bookings), ADDPlus+ must match the **UI grammar and robustness**, not copy the exact domain metric.
11	
12	---
13

16	### 1.1 Web surfaces in scope
17	- **Vendor**: `/dashboard`, `/products`, `/orders`, `/compliance`, `/earnings`, `/store`

167	- Module header
