This document is the **acceptance matrix** used to bring ADDPlus+ up to the same product-quality standard as **Solera**, **Edifice**, and **CaspaHub**.

**Strict parity** means:
- ADDPlus+ must meet **Solera’s baseline** for dashboard composition, resilience, theming, and chart readability.
- ADDPlus+ must also meet **Edifice’s multi-module consistency** (module KPI/data panel/quick links primitives).
- ADDPlus+ must also meet **CaspaHub’s ops-first dashboard patterns** (events/ops paneling, action affordances).

Where a benchmark feature is **domain-specific** (e.g., patients vs students vs bookings), ADDPlus+ must match the **UI grammar and robustness**, not copy the exact domain metric.

---

## 1) Scope & Surfaces (must be true)

### 1.1 Web surfaces in scope
- **Vendor**: `/dashboard`, `/products`, `/orders`, `/compliance`, `/earnings`, `/store`
- **Admin**: `/admin`, `/admin/vendors`, `/admin/orders`, `/admin/disputes`, `/admin/fund`, `/admin/compliance`, `/admin/insights`
- **Customer**: `/account`, `/account/orders`

### 1.2 Non-negotiable policies
- **No silent mock fallbacks** on any authenticated dashboard surface.
- Every dashboard surface has explicit **loading**, **error**, **empty**, and **success** states.

Reference intent docs:
- `docs/ADMIN_DASHBOARD_PRD.md`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`

---

## 2) Dashboard UX Parity (Solera baseline)

### 2.1 Layout grammar
For every dashboard overview:
- **PageHeader** (title + short subtitle + primary action)
- KPI row (4-up, or 2-up on small screens)
- 2-column analytic blocks (trend/chart + events/list panel)
- Dense, scan-first spacing and consistent typography tiers

Benchmark references:
- Solera `src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx`
- Solera `src/components/layout/page-header.tsx`
- Solera `src/components/dashboard/dashboard-sections.tsx`

### 2.2 KPI card grammar
Each KPI card:
- label, value, optional hint
- click-through where relevant
- consistent hover/active affordances (`card-hover`)

Benchmark reference:
- Edifice `src/components/modules/module-kpi-grid.tsx`
- Solera `src/components/dashboard/kpi-row.tsx`

### 2.3 Events + ops paneling
Each dashboard has at least one “events” panel that:
- renders empty state copy + CTA
- supports quick actions without leaving the page (where appropriate)
- maintains readability in both themes

Benchmark reference:
- CaspaHub `src/components/dashboard/events-and-panel.tsx`

### 2.4 Data freshness and honesty
- Dashboard data should degrade safely if one query fails (partial render, not blank page).
- Show “freshness” signals where meaningful (last updated / offline banner).

Benchmark reference:
- Solera `src/lib/dashboard/data.ts` (safeQuery fallbacks + aggregate-first approach)

---

## 3) Resilience States Parity (Solera baseline)

### 3.1 Route-group boundaries
Authenticated dashboard pages MUST have:
- route-group `loading.tsx`
- route-group `error.tsx` with recovery via `reset()`

ADDPlus+ references:
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/loading.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/error.tsx`

### 3.2 Page-local loading & retry
Each dashboard page:
- uses a consistent `LoadingSkeleton` on first load
- uses a consistent `ErrorCard` with **Retry**
- never shows stale data without indicating refresh state

---

## 4) Navigation + Route Integrity Parity (All three)

### 4.1 Canonical routes
- No links, redirects, or router pushes may point to non-existent routes.
- Sidebar and mobile nav must be consistent with RBAC route-module mapping.

ADDPlus+ references:
- `apps/web/src/lib/rbac-routes.ts`
- `apps/web/src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/layout/mobile-nav.tsx`

### 4.2 Role-to-surface correctness
- Vendor sees vendor surfaces; admin sees admin surfaces; customer is never routed to a vendor-only dashboard.
- Forbidden access must redirect to a safe surface with an explicit error indicator.

ADDPlus+ references:
- `apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts`
- `apps/web/src/middleware.ts`

---

## 5) Theme & Token Parity (Solera baseline)

### 5.1 Token-only styling
- No hardcoded grays/reds for core surfaces unless semantic intent requires it.
- All cards, tables, charts must be readable in light/dark using CSS variables.

Benchmark references:
- Solera `src/app/globals.css`
- Edifice `src/app/globals.css`
- CaspaHub `src/app/globals.css`

ADDPlus+ reference:
- `apps/web/src/app/globals.css`

---

## 6) Charts Parity (Solera baseline)

### 6.1 Hydration-safe charts
- Recharts render must be guarded behind a mount gate (no hydration mismatch).

Benchmark reference:
- Solera `src/components/charts/chart-mount.tsx`

### 6.2 Theme-aware chart palette
- Axis/grid/track colors must be derived from theme tokens.
- Charts must remain legible and consistent in light/dark.

Benchmark reference:
- Solera `src/lib/chart-theme.ts`

---

## 7) Data Contract Parity (All three standard)

### 7.1 Typed view-model contracts
- Each dashboard surface must have typed DTO/view-model contracts.
- Avoid `any` for dashboard “root” data blobs; prefer `DashboardData`-style shape.

Benchmark reference:
- Solera `src/lib/dashboard/data.ts` exports `DashboardData`

ADDPlus+ target:
- `apps/web/src/lib/dashboard/*` (to be created as part of parity work)

### 7.2 Aggregate-first dashboard queries
- Prefer small targeted aggregates over “load everything then compute”.
- For multi-panel dashboards, fetch in parallel and allow safe partial fallbacks.

---

## 8) Module-level Consistency (Edifice standard)

Where ADDPlus+ has multiple admin/vendor modules, each module page should follow a consistent composition pattern:
- Module header
- Module KPI grid
- Module data panel (scrollable, standardized table/list)
- Module quick links (contextual)

Benchmark references:
- Edifice `src/components/modules/module-kpi-grid.tsx`
- Edifice `src/components/modules/module-data-panel.tsx`
- Edifice `src/components/modules/module-quick-links.tsx`

---

## 9) Verification Matrix (release gate)

For each role, verify the following in **light** and **dark**:

### 9.1 Vendor
- `/dashboard` loads, primary CTA works, no dead links
- `/products` list/create/edit flows are coherent, errors are honest
- `/orders` list + status actions work, clear empty state
- `/compliance` renders score and history
- `/earnings` renders escrow and payout history
- `/store` renders profile settings

### 9.2 Admin / platform_admin
- `/admin` overview shows health metrics
- `/admin/vendors` moderation flows work
- `/admin/orders` and `/admin/disputes` operational flows work
- `/admin/fund` and `/admin/compliance` render consistent panels

### 9.3 Customer
- `/account` and `/account/orders` are correct destinations
- Customer is never routed into vendor-only pages

---

## 10) Completion Definition

Strict parity for dashboards is reached when:
- All criteria in Sections **2–9** pass for all roles, both themes.
- No route or RBAC mismatches remain.
- No stale/duplicate dashboard shell exists that can drift from production behavior.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sync API env vars to Render addplus-api (per-key PUT — does not wipe other vars).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="${1:-$ROOT/apps/api/.env}"
NO_DEPLOY="${2:-}"
if [[ "$ENV_FILE" == "--no-deploy" ]]; then
  NO_DEPLOY="--no-deploy"
  ENV_FILE="$ROOT/apps/api/.env"
fi
CONFIG="$ROOT/.render/config.yaml"
SERVICE_ID="$(grep '^service_id:' "$CONFIG" | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '"')"

if [[ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  echo "Missing env file: $ENV_FILE"
  exit 1
fi

RENDER_KEY="$(python3 -c "import yaml; print(yaml.safe_load(open('$HOME/.render/cli.yaml'))['api']['key'])")"

set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$ENV_FILE"
set +a

# Production overrides (match render.yaml + Vercel)
export NODE_ENV="${NODE_ENV:-production}"
export JWT_ISSUER="${JWT_ISSUER:-addplus-api}"
export JWT_AUDIENCE="${JWT_AUDIENCE:-addplus-client}"
export CLIENT_URL="https://addplus.vercel.app"

<result># ADDPlus+ Platform Layer Audit — Findings

Scope covered: every file under `src/db/**`, `src/lib/actions/**`, all listed `src/lib/**` files, `src/lib/{messages,offline,stream,sync}/**`, `src/instrumentation.ts`, `src/sw.ts`, all 5 API routes, both migration scripts, `drizzle.config.ts`, plus `next.config.js`, `.env.example`, root `vercel.json`/`render.yaml` for cross-checks.

## Security findings

**1. CRITICAL — Unauthenticated server action returns password hashes and reset tokens for any user**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/profile.ts:30-34`. `getProfileForUser(userId)` is exported from a `"use server"` module with zero auth checks and does `SELECT *` from `globalUsers`, returning `passwordHash`, `passwordResetToken`, `verificationToken`, `sessionVersion` to the caller for ANY `userId` argument. Its action ID ships in the client bundle (`src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:11,23` imports it), so anyone can POST to it directly; a leaked reset token = full account takeover via `/reset-password?token=`.

**2. HIGH — Unauthenticated `sendVerificationEmail` action: email verification bypass, token disclosure, mail bombing**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/auth-email.ts:25-50`. Exported server action taking arbitrary `(userId, email, name)`: (a) overwrites any victim's `verificationToken`; (b) sends the verification link to an attacker-chosen address, letting the attacker verify someone else's email; (c) on send failure it **returns the verification link in the action result** (lines 46-48) — attacker forces failure and reads the token; (d) has no rate limit of its own (the limits in `registerUser`/`resendVerificationEmail` are trivially bypassed by calling the action directly) → unlimited emails from Brevo sender reputation.

**3. HIGH — Tenant team data leak: `getTeamMembers` returns full user rows including password hashes**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/settings.ts:386-397` joins `tenantMemberships` with `globalUsers` and returns entire rows (incl. `passwordHash`, reset tokens) to the browser of anyone passing `requireTenantAction("settings","read")`.

**4. HIGH — RBAC matrix is legacy marketplace roles; all invited staff roles are locked out of everything**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts:26-57` defines roles `platform_admin|admin|vendor|customer`, but tenants actually use `super_admin|admin|pharmacist|cashier|doctor|nurse|receptionist` (`settings.ts:21-28`, seeded `tenant.ts:457,562`). Only `super_admin`→`admin` is normalized (rbac.ts:61). Every other invited role fails `requirePermission` in `requireTenantAction` (`actions/context.ts:47`) — pharmacists/cashiers can't read messages, fetch notifications, or get Stream tokens (`src/app/api/stream/token/route.ts:14`). Conversely `vendor`/`customer` in the MATRIX don't exist in this system. Masked by `ignoreBuildErrors`.

**5. MEDIUM — Unauthenticated cross-tenant subscription status read**
`/home/paypop-os/../addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/billing.ts:21-29` — `getTenantSubscription(tenantId)` is an exported `"use server"` function with no auth check returning any tenant's subscription row (status, period dates).

**6. MEDIUM — Unauthenticated pending profile-change lookup**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/profile.ts:36-51` — `getPendingProfileChange(userId, tenantId)` exported with no auth check.

**7. MEDIUM — `updateMemberRole` accepts arbitrary role strings on direct invocation**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/settings.ts:215-244` — role validation lives only in the form wrapper (`updateMemberRoleForm`); the exported action itself will persist any string (e.g. `super_admin`, or garbage) to metadata + tenant DBs.

**8. MEDIUM — No plan `maxUsers` enforcement anywhere**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/plans.ts` only implements `assertCanAddBranch`/clinic gating. Neither `inviteTeamMember` nor `acceptInvitationRecord` (`invitations.ts:63-154`) checks member count against `maxUsers`, so Starter tenants can add unlimited users.

**9. MEDIUM — Rate limiting keyed on spoofable `x-forwarded-for`; DDL per call**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/rate-limit.ts:25-32,40` — client-supplied XFF trusted blindly (safe on Vercel, bypassable anywhere else); `ensureTable()` runs `CREATE TABLE` on **every** rate-limit call; SELECT-then-UPDATE is non-atomic (concurrent requests overshoot the limit). Also `resetPassword` (`auth-email.ts:107-139`) has no rate limit at all.

**10. MEDIUM — Crypto: single derived key, no rotation/fallback path; prod hard-fail gated on Vercel**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/crypto.ts:6-8` derives AES-256-GCM key via SHA-256 of `ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? AUTH_SECRET` (`env.ts:24-33`). IV is random 12 bytes per encryption (good), but there is no fallback-key list: rotating either secret permanently bricks every tenant's `dbTokenEncrypted`. Dev fallback constant `"dev-only-encryption-key-not-for-production"`. Separately `assertEnv()` (`env.ts:17-19`) only throws when `NODE_ENV=production && VERCEL_ENV` — a self-hosted prod deploy silently runs without required env.

**11. MEDIUM — Web-push subsystem completely unwired**
No `/api/messages/push` route exists, but `src/components/messages/push-prompt.tsx:33,43` fetches it; `savePushSubscription`/`removePushSubscription`/`getVapidPublicKey` (`src/lib/messages/push.ts`) have zero callers. `src/sw.ts` is never compiled: `serwist`/`@serwist/next` are absent from `package.json` and `next.config.js` has no Serwist wrapper; no `sw.js` exists in `public/`, so `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` never resolves. Push notifications cannot work end-to-end.

**12. MEDIUM — NextAuth JWT callback hits the DB 2–3x per request**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:129-166` runs unconditionally on every `jwt` callback (no `trigger === "signIn"/"update"` check, no caching): one `global_users` select, `resolveActiveMembership` select, and `resolveTenantStatus` join — 3 Turso queries per request per user. Also sessionVersion mismatch (auth.ts:149-154) strips tenant claims but leaves the user signed in as a role-less identity instead of forcing sign-out.

**13. MEDIUM — Hardcoded URLs, emails, phone numbers, infra identifiers in production paths**
- `https://addplus-api.onrender.com` fallback: `src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts:7`, `src/app/api/payments/status/route.ts:7`, `src/lib/api.ts:8`.
- `http://localhost:3000` fallback for verification/reset/invite links: `auth-email.ts:21`, `settings.ts:62,142` (dead links if `APP_URL` unset).
- `https://solera.app` fallback: `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts:39`; VAPID subject `mailto:support@solerasite.vercel.app`: `src/lib/messages/push.ts:9`.
- Real personal emails committed: `.env.example:27` `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com,kennedymuritu001@gmail.com`; real Turso hostname/org `.env.example:2,4` and default org `ken-muritu` in `turso-api.ts:4`.
- Repo-root `render.yaml`: `SEED_ADMIN_PHONE=254115594826`, `BREVO_FROM=...kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com`, and PayHero callback pointed at the old app.
- Fabricated demo content still rendered on live pages: `src/lib/mockData.ts` imported by `marketplace/page.tsx`, `cart/page.tsx`, `products/[id]/page.tsx`, `vendors/[id]/page.tsx`.

**14. LOW — Webhook secret passed as URL query param**
`payhero-webhook.ts:36-45` appends `?secret=` to the PayHero callback URL (leaks into provider/access logs). The verifier itself (`timingSafeEqual`, fail-closed when secret set in prod) is sound — but note it is **never invoked anywhere** (see finding 17).

**15. LOW — Misc isolation/hygiene gaps**
Platform replies impersonate "first active staff member" of the tenant (`platform-sync.ts:71-85`); `createGroupConversation` doesn't validate member IDs exist (`actions/messages.ts:400-440`); provision lock conflates any DB error with "already in progress", and globally-unique `slug` from `slugify(businessName)` collides across tenants → second pharmacy named e.g. "Main Pharmacy" fails provisioning (`tenant.ts:528-556`); `payments/status` GET route is unauthenticated and returns payment state for guessable references.

## Billing / plans

**16. HIGH — Plan selection destroyed by legacy marketplace helper**
`completeOnboarding` passes `normalizePlanId(...)` (`actions/auth.ts:169`) which returns only `"seller"|"growth"` (`marketing-content.ts:29-31`) while the plans table seeds only `starter|professional` (`scripts/migrate-metadata.ts:176-196`) and the onboarding `<select>` offers starter/professional. Every new tenant gets a nonexistent `plan_id="seller"`; subscription confirmation regex expects `-(starter|professional)-` (`billing/payhero.ts:112`) so plan upgrades would never match the stored plan.

**17. CRITICAL — Paid subscriptions can never activate: confirmation code is dead and the webhook is proxied to the old API**
`confirmSubscriptionPayment`/`confirmSalePayment` are called only from `lib/payments/status.ts`, whose export `getPaymentStatus` has **zero callers**. The live `/api/payhero/callback` route is a pure proxy to the legacy Express API (`app/api/payhero/callback/route.ts:12-35`) and never calls `verifyPayHeroCallback` or updates the Solera metadata DB; `/api/payments/status` likewise polls the old API which knows nothing of `SUB-*` references. Additionally `lib/payments/confirm-sale.ts:5` imports the **nonexistent** module `@/lib/compliance`, and `sync/replay.ts:7-8` imports nonexistent `@/lib/actions/pharmacy` and `@/lib/actions/clinic` — these files compile only because nothing reachable imports them and `ignoreBuildErrors: true` (`next.config.js:4-8`). Net effect: users pay via STK push, subscription stays `pending`, tenant stays `trial_expired` forever.

**18. Trial enforcement**: enforced correctly server-side in `getTenantContext` → `expireTrialIfNeeded`/`expireCancelledSubscriptionIfNeeded` + `resolveTenantAccess` (`tenant.ts:78-128,196-207`, `tenant-access.ts`), independent of the middleware redirect. Users cannot self-upgrade free (no action sets `status="active"` without payment/platform admin). Minor: `resolveTenantStatus` in `auth.ts:10-31` reads raw status without expiry computation, so the JWT `tenantStatus` lags until something calls `getTenantContext`.

## Broken/dead platform plumbing (functional)

**19. CRITICAL — next.config redirect kills the entire onboarding flow**
`next.config.js:26`: `{ source: '/onboarding', destination: '/signup?type=vendor', permanent: false }` — a leftover marketplace redirect. Config redirects run ahead of middleware/pages, yet `/onboarding` is the Solera provisioning page (`src/app/onboarding/page.tsx`) and the canonical redirect target of middleware (`middleware.ts:115`), `session.ts:22,29,37,52,55`, `context.ts:17,24`, `auth.ts:92`. New users can never provision a tenant through the UI.

**20. HIGH — Two parallel auth systems; the Solera login/signup actions are dead code**
The live `/login` and `/signup` forms use the **legacy Express API** flow (`components/auth/login-form.tsx:12` → `session-client.ts` → axios `api.ts` → old API; tokens in localStorage/XOR-obfuscated storage + cookie bridge via `/api/auth/session`). The NextAuth-based `loginUser`/`registerUser` server actions (`actions/auth.ts:21-145`) — including invitation acceptance on signup and Brevo verification — are referenced by **no page or component**. Result: real users authenticate without a NextAuth session/tenant, while the whole Solera membership layer assumes one.

**21. HIGH — Offline sync is broken at every layer**
Client queues ops and POSTs to `/api/sync` (`offline/store.ts:80`) — that route doesn't exist. Background Sync tag `solera-sync` is registered (`store.ts:56-64`) but `sw.ts` has no `sync` event listener (and isn't built anyway). Server-side replay is dead: `sync/replay.ts` imports nonexistent modules; `canSyncOperation` (`sync/permissions.ts:3-11`) references modules (`pos`, `patients`, `prescriptions`, `inventory`, `clinic`) that aren't in the `Module` union, so it always returns `false` — a type hole exactly of the kind `ignoreBuildErrors` hides. `claimSyncOperation` idempotency logic itself is fine but unreachable.

## Dead / duplicated dependencies & unused exports

Unused dependencies (zero imports in `src/`):
- `react-hot-toast` (all call sites use `sonner`; `lib/toast.ts` just re-exports sonner)
- `@tanstack/react-query` — mounted in `src/components/providers.tsx`, but that Providers component itself has zero importers (root layout uses `providers/theme-provider`), and no `useQuery`/`useMutation` exists anywhere
- `@heroicons/react` (everything uses `lucide-react`)
- `react-hook-form` + `@hookform/resolvers`
- `uuid` (nanoid + `crypto.randomUUID` used)
- `@headlessui/react`
- `axios` — only used by the legacy `api.ts`/`session-client.ts` stack

<result># ADDPlus+ Platform Layer Audit — Findings

Scope covered: every file under `src/db/**`, `src/lib/actions/**`, all listed `src/lib/**` files, `src/lib/{messages,offline,stream,sync}/**`, `src/instrumentation.ts`, `src/sw.ts`, all 5 API routes, both migration scripts, `drizzle.config.ts`, plus `next.config.js`, `.env.example`, root `vercel.json`/`render.yaml` for cross-checks.

## Security findings

**1. CRITICAL — Unauthenticated server action returns password hashes and reset tokens for any user**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/profile.ts:30-34`. `getProfileForUser(userId)` is exported from a `"use server"` module with zero auth checks and does `SELECT *` from `globalUsers`, returning `passwordHash`, `passwordResetToken`, `verificationToken`, `sessionVersion` to the caller for ANY `userId` argument. Its action ID ships in the client bundle (`src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:11,23` imports it), so anyone can POST to it directly; a leaked reset token = full account takeover via `/reset-password?token=`.

**2. HIGH — Unauthenticated `sendVerificationEmail` action: email verification bypass, token disclosure, mail bombing**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/auth-email.ts:25-50`. Exported server action taking arbitrary `(userId, email, name)`: (a) overwrites any victim's `verificationToken`; (b) sends the verification link to an attacker-chosen address, letting the attacker verify someone else's email; (c) on send failure it **returns the verification link in the action result** (lines 46-48) — attacker forces failure and reads the token; (d) has no rate limit of its own (the limits in `registerUser`/`resendVerificationEmail` are trivially bypassed by calling the action directly) → unlimited emails from Brevo sender reputation.

**3. HIGH — Tenant team data leak: `getTeamMembers` returns full user rows including password hashes**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/settings.ts:386-397` joins `tenantMemberships` with `globalUsers` and returns entire rows (incl. `passwordHash`, reset tokens) to the browser of anyone passing `requireTenantAction("settings","read")`.

**4. HIGH — RBAC matrix is legacy marketplace roles; all invited staff roles are locked out of everything**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts:26-57` defines roles `platform_admin|admin|vendor|customer`, but tenants actually use `super_admin|admin|pharmacist|cashier|doctor|nurse|receptionist` (`settings.ts:21-28`, seeded `tenant.ts:457,562`). Only `super_admin`→`admin` is normalized (rbac.ts:61). Every other invited role fails `requirePermission` in `requireTenantAction` (`actions/context.ts:47`) — pharmacists/cashiers can't read messages, fetch notifications, or get Stream tokens (`src/app/api/stream/token/route.ts:14`). Conversely `vendor`/`customer` in the MATRIX don't exist in this system. Masked by `ignoreBuildErrors`.

**5. MEDIUM — Unauthenticated cross-tenant subscription status read**
`/home/paypop-os/../addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/billing.ts:21-29` — `getTenantSubscription(tenantId)` is an exported `"use server"` function with no auth check returning any tenant's subscription row (status, period dates).

**6. MEDIUM — Unauthenticated pending profile-change lookup**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/profile.ts:36-51` — `getPendingProfileChange(userId, tenantId)` exported with no auth check.

**7. MEDIUM — `updateMemberRole` accepts arbitrary role strings on direct invocation**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/actions/settings.ts:215-244` — role validation lives only in the form wrapper (`updateMemberRoleForm`); the exported action itself will persist any string (e.g. `super_admin`, or garbage) to metadata + tenant DBs.

**8. MEDIUM — No plan `maxUsers` enforcement anywhere**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/plans.ts` only implements `assertCanAddBranch`/clinic gating. Neither `inviteTeamMember` nor `acceptInvitationRecord` (`invitations.ts:63-154`) checks member count against `maxUsers`, so Starter tenants can add unlimited users.

**9. MEDIUM — Rate limiting keyed on spoofable `x-forwarded-for`; DDL per call**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/rate-limit.ts:25-32,40` — client-supplied XFF trusted blindly (safe on Vercel, bypassable anywhere else); `ensureTable()` runs `CREATE TABLE` on **every** rate-limit call; SELECT-then-UPDATE is non-atomic (concurrent requests overshoot the limit). Also `resetPassword` (`auth-email.ts:107-139`) has no rate limit at all.

**10. MEDIUM — Crypto: single derived key, no rotation/fallback path; prod hard-fail gated on Vercel**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/crypto.ts:6-8` derives AES-256-GCM key via SHA-256 of `ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? AUTH_SECRET` (`env.ts:24-33`). IV is random 12 bytes per encryption (good), but there is no fallback-key list: rotating either secret permanently bricks every tenant's `dbTokenEncrypted`. Dev fallback constant `"dev-only-encryption-key-not-for-production"`. Separately `assertEnv()` (`env.ts:17-19`) only throws when `NODE_ENV=production && VERCEL_ENV` — a self-hosted prod deploy silently runs without required env.

**11. MEDIUM — Web-push subsystem completely unwired**
No `/api/messages/push` route exists, but `src/components/messages/push-prompt.tsx:33,43` fetches it; `savePushSubscription`/`removePushSubscription`/`getVapidPublicKey` (`src/lib/messages/push.ts`) have zero callers. `src/sw.ts` is never compiled: `serwist`/`@serwist/next` are absent from `package.json` and `next.config.js` has no Serwist wrapper; no `sw.js` exists in `public/`, so `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` never resolves. Push notifications cannot work end-to-end.

**12. MEDIUM — NextAuth JWT callback hits the DB 2–3x per request**
`/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:129-166` runs unconditionally on every `jwt` callback (no `trigger === "signIn"/"update"` check, no caching): one `global_users` select, `resolveActiveMembership` select, and `resolveTenantStatus` join — 3 Turso queries per request per user. Also sessionVersion mismatch (auth.ts:149-154) strips tenant claims but leaves the user signed in as a role-less identity instead of forcing sign-out.

**13. MEDIUM — Hardcoded URLs, emails, phone numbers, infra identifiers in production paths**
- `https://addplus-api.onrender.com` fallback: `src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts:7`, `src/app/api/payments/status/route.ts:7`, `src/lib/api.ts:8`.
- `http://localhost:3000` fallback for verification/reset/invite links: `auth-email.ts:21`, `settings.ts:62,142` (dead links if `APP_URL` unset).
- `https://solera.app` fallback: `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts:39`; VAPID subject `mailto:support@solerasite.vercel.app`: `src/lib/messages/push.ts:9`.
- Real personal emails committed: `.env.example:27` `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com,kennedymuritu001@gmail.com`; real Turso hostname/org `.env.example:2,4` and default org `ken-muritu` in `turso-api.ts:4`.
- Repo-root `render.yaml`: `SEED_ADMIN_PHONE=254115594826`, `BREVO_FROM=...kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com`, and PayHero callback pointed at the old app.
- Fabricated demo content still rendered on live pages: `src/lib/mockData.ts` imported by `marketplace/page.tsx`, `cart/page.tsx`, `products/[id]/page.tsx`, `vendors/[id]/page.tsx`.

**14. LOW — Webhook secret passed as URL query param**
`payhero-webhook.ts:36-45` appends `?secret=` to the PayHero callback URL (leaks into provider/access logs). The verifier itself (`timingSafeEqual`, fail-closed when secret set in prod) is sound — but note it is **never invoked anywhere** (see finding 17).

**15. LOW — Misc isolation/hygiene gaps**
Platform replies impersonate "first active staff member" of the tenant (`platform-sync.ts:71-85`); `createGroupConversation` doesn't validate member IDs exist (`actions/messages.ts:400-440`); provision lock conflates any DB error with "already in progress", and globally-unique `slug` from `slugify(businessName)` collides across tenants → second pharmacy named e.g. "Main Pharmacy" fails provisioning (`tenant.ts:528-556`); `payments/status` GET route is unauthenticated and returns payment state for guessable references.

## Billing / plans

**16. HIGH — Plan selection destroyed by legacy marketplace helper**
`completeOnboarding` passes `normalizePlanId(...)` (`actions/auth.ts:169`) which returns only `"seller"|"growth"` (`marketing-content.ts:29-31`) while the plans table seeds only `starter|professional` (`scripts/migrate-metadata.ts:176-196`) and the onboarding `<select>` offers starter/professional. Every new tenant gets a nonexistent `plan_id="seller"`; subscription confirmation regex expects `-(starter|professional)-` (`billing/payhero.ts:112`) so plan upgrades would never match the stored plan.

**17. CRITICAL — Paid subscriptions can never activate: confirmation code is dead and the webhook is proxied to the old API**
`confirmSubscriptionPayment`/`confirmSalePayment` are called only from `lib/payments/status.ts`, whose export `getPaymentStatus` has **zero callers**. The live `/api/payhero/callback` route is a pure proxy to the legacy Express API (`app/api/payhero/callback/route.ts:12-35`) and never calls `verifyPayHeroCallback` or updates the Solera metadata DB; `/api/payments/status` likewise polls the old API which knows nothing of `SUB-*` references. Additionally `lib/payments/confirm-sale.ts:5` imports the **nonexistent** module `@/lib/compliance`, and `sync/replay.ts:7-8` imports nonexistent `@/lib/actions/pharmacy` and `@/lib/actions/clinic` — these files compile only because nothing reachable imports them and `ignoreBuildErrors: true` (`next.config.js:4-8`). Net effect: users pay via STK push, subscription stays `pending`, tenant stays `trial_expired` forever.

**18. Trial enforcement**: enforced correctly server-side in `getTenantContext` → `expireTrialIfNeeded`/`expireCancelledSubscriptionIfNeeded` + `resolveTenantAccess` (`tenant.ts:78-128,196-207`, `tenant-access.ts`), independent of the middleware redirect. Users cannot self-upgrade free (no action sets `status="active"` without payment/platform admin). Minor: `resolveTenantStatus` in `auth.ts:10-31` reads raw status without expiry computation, so the JWT `tenantStatus` lags until something calls `getTenantContext`.

## Broken/dead platform plumbing (functional)

**19. CRITICAL — next.config redirect kills the entire onboarding flow**
`next.config.js:26`: `{ source: '/onboarding', destination: '/signup?type=vendor', permanent: false }` — a leftover marketplace redirect. Config redirects run ahead of middleware/pages, yet `/onboarding` is the Solera provisioning page (`src/app/onboarding/page.tsx`) and the canonical redirect target of middleware (`middleware.ts:115`), `session.ts:22,29,37,52,55`, `context.ts:17,24`, `auth.ts:92`. New users can never provision a tenant through the UI.

**20. HIGH — Two parallel auth systems; the Solera login/signup actions are dead code**
The live `/login` and `/signup` forms use the **legacy Express API** flow (`components/auth/login-form.tsx:12` → `session-client.ts` → axios `api.ts` → old API; tokens in localStorage/XOR-obfuscated storage + cookie bridge via `/api/auth/session`). The NextAuth-based `loginUser`/`registerUser` server actions (`actions/auth.ts:21-145`) — including invitation acceptance on signup and Brevo verification — are referenced by **no page or component**. Result: real users authenticate without a NextAuth session/tenant, while the whole Solera membership layer assumes one.

**21. HIGH — Offline sync is broken at every layer**
Client queues ops and POSTs to `/api/sync` (`offline/store.ts:80`) — that route doesn't exist. Background Sync tag `solera-sync` is registered (`store.ts:56-64`) but `sw.ts` has no `sync` event listener (and isn't built anyway). Server-side replay is dead: `sync/replay.ts` imports nonexistent modules; `canSyncOperation` (`sync/permissions.ts:3-11`) references modules (`pos`, `patients`, `prescriptions`, `inventory`, `clinic`) that aren't in the `Module` union, so it always returns `false` — a type hole exactly of the kind `ignoreBuildErrors` hides. `claimSyncOperation` idempotency logic itself is fine but unreachable.

## Dead / duplicated dependencies & unused exports

Unused dependencies (zero imports in `src/`):

# ADDPlus+ Mobile Audit — 2026-08-25

Scope: every file under `/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/mobile` (17 source/config files), cross-referenced against `/home/pop-os/addplus/apps/api/src/routes/*`, `apps/api/src/services/authService.ts`, `.github/workflows/build-apk.yml`, and `render.yaml`.

## Re-verification of June 2026 findings

**1. CartScreen checkout fail-open — STILL BROKEN (CRITICAL)**
`src/screens/CartScreen.tsx:69-73` — the bare `catch` fabricates `ORD-${Date.now()...}`, sets `step('payment')`, clears the cart. Any failure (network down, 401, PayHero outage) shows "Payment Initiated! Check your M-Pesa phone..." with no order created. User believes they paid; nothing exists server-side. `orderId` (line 28) is written but never rendered — even the fake ID isn't shown.

**2. HomeScreen search non-functional; chips don't filter — STILL BROKEN**
`src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx:118-121` — the "search bar" is a static `View`+`Text` placeholder; there is no `TextInput`, no press handler. `HomeScreen.tsx:130-137` — every category chip just calls `navigation.navigate('Marketplace')` with no params; Marketplace never reads route params either.

**3. Marketplace infinite scroll breaks on mock data — STILL BROKEN, worse than reported**
`src/screens/MarketplaceScreen.tsx:70` — `if (fetched.length === 0) throw new Error('empty')` treats a legitimately-empty page (end of list, or filtered result with no hits on the real API) as an error. The catch (`:76-86`) then **appends mock products to already-loaded real products**, sets `total = mock.length`, and on reset replaces real data with the 17-item mock set. Scrolling to the end of real catalog injects fake listings.

**4. Wishlist heart Alert-only, no store — STILL BROKEN**
`src/screens/ProductDetailScreen.tsx:220-224` — heart button fires `Alert.alert('Saved', 'Added to wishlist')`. There is no wishlist store anywhere (`src/store/` contains only `useAuthStore.ts` and `useCartStore.ts`). Nothing is saved.

**5. ProfileScreen menu stubs — STILL BROKEN (now three)**
`src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx:51` Saved Items `onPress: () => {}`; `:53` Buyer Protection `() => {}`; `:54` Help & Support `() => {}`. All three render as tappable rows that do nothing.

**6. ProductDetailScreen/VendorStoreScreen no offline fallback — STILL BROKEN**
`src/screens/ProductDetailScreen.tsx:43-47` — catch only `console.error`s; product stays null → "Product not found". `src/screens/VendorStoreScreen.tsx:39-40,56` — same pattern → "Vendor not found". Because of finding #7 below, this is not an edge case: *every* product/store tap shows "not found".

**7. Push token registration errors swallowed — STILL BROKEN**
`App.tsx:103` — `authApi.registerPushToken(token).catch(() => {})`. Additionally `App.tsx:69-87` — `registerForPushNotificationsAsync()` itself has no catch on its returned promise, so a rejection inside `getExpoPushTokenAsync()` (guaranteed here, see finding #12's invalid projectId) becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Android standalone push also needs FCM credentials the `expo-notifications` plugin config (app.json:33) doesn't supply.

**8. expo-image-picker declared but never used — STILL BROKEN**
`package.json:26` declares `expo-image-picker ~14.7.1`, `app.json:32` registers it as a config plugin; grep of `src/` and `App.tsx` finds zero `ImagePicker` references.

**9. React Query mounted, zero hooks — STILL BROKEN**
`App.tsx:9,28,108` create and mount `QueryClientProvider`; grep confirms no `useQuery`/`useMutation`/`useInfiniteQuery` anywhere in the app. Pure dead weight (~every fetch is hand-rolled useState/useEffect).

**10. eas.projectId placeholder — STILL BROKEN**
`app.json:37` — `"projectId": "addplus-ke"`. Not a UUID; `eas init` was never run. Breaks EAS project association, `getExpoPushTokenAsync()` (throws "projectId is invalid"), and OTA updates.

**11. GitHub Actions references missing package-lock — STILL BROKEN**
`.github/workflows/build-apk.yml:32` — `cache-dependency-path: apps/mobile/package-lock.json`. That file does not exist (the only lockfile is the root `/home/pop-os/addplus/package-lock.json`). The setup-node step fails before EAS ever runs; `npm install` at `:43` is also unreproducible without a lockfile.

## New findings

**12. CRITICAL — Mobile login payload contradicts backend contract; every login fails with 400**
`src/lib/api.ts:59` sends `{ phone, password }`; `src/screens/LoginScreen.tsx:38` calls it. Backend `apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:35-38` validates `{ identifier, password }` via strict Zod `loginSchema.parse` (`:72`) → ZodError → 400 "Validation error" on **every** attempt. The July pivot renamed the field to `identifier` (email-or-phone, `authService.ts:102-110`) and mobile was never updated. Response shapes otherwise match (`buildAuthResponse` returns top-level `user`/`accessToken`/`refreshToken`, so `LoginScreen.tsx:44` would work — if the request ever passed validation), and `needsPasswordSetup` (`auth.ts:74` + `authService.ts:122`) matches `LoginScreen.tsx:40`.

**13. CRITICAL — API base URL points at a host that isn't the deployed backend**
`app.json:39` and the hardcoded fallback `src/lib/api.ts:5-7` both use `https://api.addplus.co.ke/v1`. Production is Render service `addplus-api` → `https://addplus-api.onrender.com/v1` (render.yaml service name; web app confirms at `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts:7`). # ADDPlus+ — Full-Picture Audit Report

**Confirmed: I have the complete picture.** Every past session was mined for context; the repo (105 commits, HEAD `1fdf375`) was cloned to `~/addplus` and read area-by-area — I personally line-read the entire Express API (all 10 route modules, 12 services, middleware, schema, crons, deploy configs), and four parallel deep-audits covered the web platform layer, every page/component, the mobile app, and the live deployments with unauthenticated probing. Here is everything, ranked.

---

## ⚠️ The one structural truth that explains most of this

In July 2026, your **Solera pharmacy platform was grafted into ADDPlus+** — NextAuth v5, a Drizzle metadata Turso DB, per-tenant databases whose schema is literally *pharmacy* tables (`patients`, `prescriptions`, PPB license numbers), PayHero SaaS billing, Stream Chat. Your own in-repo skill doc says ADDPlus+ "shares only the author" with Solera and warns not to port those patterns here — but they were ported. **The grafted layer is ~90% dead code**: live login/signup/orders all run on the legacy Express-API path; nothing real ever touches NextAuth or tenant DBs. It added critical vulnerabilities, killed onboarding, and left Solera pharmacy text all over production — without serving a single live flow.

---

## 🔴 CRITICAL — 20 findings

**Security**
| # | Finding | Where |
|---|---------|-------|
| 1 | Unauthenticated server action returns **password hashes + reset/verification tokens** for any user ID | `lib/actions/profile.ts:30` (`getProfileForUser`) |
| 2 | Account-takeover chain: `/v1/auth/password/setup` sets passwords on passwordless admin/vendor accounts unauthenticated; login's `needsPasswordSetup:true` response tells attackers which phones qualify | `authService.ts:102-168` |
| 3 | Path traversal → arbitrary file read on API server (`%2e%2e%2f` in upload path params) | `routes/uploads.ts:22-30` |
| 4 | `sendVerificationEmail` action lets anyone verify someone else's email, forces failure to **read the token out of the response**, and mail-bombs Brevo | `lib/actions/auth-email.ts:25-50` |
| 5 | Team-settings action returns full user rows incl. password hashes to the browser | `lib/actions/settings.ts:386-397` |

**Money**
| # | Finding | Where |
|---|---------|-------|
| 6 | Profit-share cron re-pays the **entire lifetime levy pool every Monday** (contributions never marked distributed) | `crons.ts:227-297` |
| 7 | A duplicate/late "failed" callback **cancels an already-paid order** (no status guard) | `paymentConfirmationService.ts:106-114` |
| 8 | Platform subscriptions can never activate — confirmation code unreachable, webhook proxied to old API that ignores `SUB-*` refs | platform billing stack |
| 9 | Mobile checkout **fail-open**: any API error fabricates "Payment Initiated!" with no order created | `CartScreen.tsx:69-73` |

**Functional kill-switches**
| # | Finding | Where |
|---|---------|-------|
| 10 | `/onboarding` redirect loop — middleware bounces tenant-less users to a page `next.config.js` redirects away; provisioning impossible | `next.config.js:26` + `middleware.ts:115` |
| 11 | Mobile sends `{phone}`; API demands `{identifier}` → **every mobile login 400s** | `api.ts:59` vs `routes/auth.ts:35` |
| 12 | Mobile base URL `api.addplus.co.ke` doesn't resolve — production is `addplus-api.onrender.com`; app silently becomes a mock demo | `app.json:39` |
| 13 | Messaging transport hits 5 nonexistent routes; EventSource reconnect-hammers a 404 every 2s forever | `use-message-stream.ts`, `messages-client.tsx` |
| 14 | Status page health-checks nonexistent `/api/health` → production always shows "Service disruption detected" | `status/page.tsx:15-27` |
| 15 | COD checkout requires an M-Pesa number from an input that only renders for M-Pesa → **COD impossible** | `cart/page.tsx:82,712` |
| 16 | Mobile `assets/` folder missing entirely while `app.json` references 4 files in it → EAS builds impossible | `apps/mobile` |
| 17 | Latent production payment failure: Daraja callbacks require `x-mpesa-signature`, which Safaricom never sends → real prod callbacks rejected unless sandbox mode | `mpesaService.ts:35-59` |

**Brand/legal exposure (live on production right now)**
| # | Finding | Where |
|---|---------|-------|
| 18 | `/privacy` + `/terms` are verbatim **Solera pharmacy legal pages** ("patient records", "prescriptions", `privacy@solera.app`) published as ADDPlus+ policy | live site |
| 19 | Onboarding page says "Set up your **pharmacy**", asks for "PPB License number", button reads "**Launch Solera**"; plans priced KES 6,500/13,000 (Solera) contradict pricing page (Seller/Growth) | `onboarding/page.tsx` |
| 20 | Contact form is a bare `mailto:hello@solera.app` stub — zero leads captured, addressed to the forked-away product | `contact-form.tsx:19` |

---

## 🟠 HIGH — headline items (30 total)

**Architecture:** dual auth systems where live users bypass NextAuth entirely (#21); RBAC matrix roles (`vendor/customer`) match none of the seeded staff roles (`super_admin/pharmacist/cashier…`) so invited staff are locked out of everything (#22); two incompatible plan systems — signup writes `plan_id="seller"|"growth"` into a table seeded only with `starter|professional`, so upgrades can never match (#23); offline sync broken at every layer (`/api/sync` route doesn't exist, replay imports phantom modules, service worker never compiled despite PWA manifest) (#24).

**Money-path carryovers from June, still open:** stock never decremented on purchase → overselling (#25); escrow stuck forever if vendor never dispatches (#26); B2C payout refs stored as `conversationID` but reconciled against `TransactionID` → payouts never confirm (#27); admin dispute refund crashes on Prisma unknown-field `refund_amount` vs `refund_amount_cents` (#28); escrow releases non-transactional; `resolved_release` marks ledger released with no actual B2C.

**API gaps:** drafts leak publicly via `GET /v1/products?include_drafts=true` (#29); `forgot-password` response shape enables email enumeration (#30).

**Web UX:** invalid Tailwind class `bg-[var(--brand-primary-light)]0` ×17 → invisible add-to-cart buttons, badges, progress bars (#31); 404 page white-on-white in light mode (#32); variant price ignored at add-to-cart (#33); compare→cart hardcodes `vendorId:'vendor-1'` (#34); navbar desktop search dead since May (#35); marketplace ignores `?search=`/`?category=`/`?q=` — three different param names across entry points (#36); pickup/boda selections never sent in order payload + client-computed discount trusted by server (#37); store photo uploads to wrong endpoint (#38); wishlist hearts decorative on grids (#39); tracking page = static Jan-2024 mock with fabricated demo-order fallback, dead support buttons, orphaned (#40); notification bell wired to pharmacy links (`/prescriptions` → 404s) and requires a tenant marketplace users will never have (#41); back-in-stock promises SMS/email, stores localStorage only (#42); trial-expired CTA dead-ends into a "coming soon" settings stub while real billing UI sits orphaned (#43); WhatsApp chat renders `<a href="">` reload for every real vendor (#44).

**Mobile:** four screens show fabricated data as real — fake delivered orders with working-looking dispute buttons, **KES 1.85M fake vendor earnings**, mock products injected when you scroll to catalog end (#45); access tokens expire in 15 min with zero refresh handling → permanent 401s masked by mock data (#46); tokens plaintext in AsyncStorage (#47); cart buttons dead on product/vendor pages (React Navigation can't navigate downward) (#48); vendor dashboard `goBack()` on mount for vendors whose session predates their store (#49); CI workflow dies on missing lockfile + placeholder EAS projectId (#50).

**Infra:** zero security headers on the entire web tier (API has them all) (#51); NextAuth JWT callback = 2–3 Turso queries per request per user (#52).

---

## 🟡 MEDIUM / LOW — compressed (70+ more)

Sanitizer corrupts legit input ("B&B", "Mama & Kids" trip command-injection regexes; apostrophes stripped) • fee story contradicts itself (cart KES 150 flat vs homepage 5% vs register 10% vs pricing 8%/6%) • fake reviews/Q&A keyed to legacy IDs p1–p15 render for those IDs while real products show empty • invented testimonials/stats ("200+ vendors", "KES 2M+") • robots.txt → non-resolving `addplus.co.ke`, no sitemap anywhere • no og:image despite `summary_large_image` • broken Unsplash hotlinks in live catalog • NaN renders (compliance %, KES NaN) • cart can't change/remove variant items • SLA copy mismatch 48h vs 72h • dev copy in prod ("placeholder link for testing", "Dev OTP shown on login") • Solera leftovers in storage keys, log prefixes, nav labels ("Prescriptions: Rx"), Brevo widget teal + old account ID • public API exposes vendor `compliance_score`/`fine_balance`/personal phone • dead deps: react-hot-toast, react-query, heroicons, react-hook-form, uuid, headlessui, dual theme engines/toast/billing/messaging stacks • `barcode-display.tsx` imports modules that don't exist (survives via `ignoreBuildErrors:true`) • charts components unused despite recharts dep • `purge-users-turso.sh` nukes ALL orders/escrow, not just users • README/docs stats frozen at June; SECURITY_AUDIT claims contradicted by code • `.netlify` orphan • CORS allows any `*.vercel.app` with credentials • no timeouts on any external HTTP call • views increment on every read.

---

## ✅ What genuinely works (so we don't fix what isn't broken)

Live catalog + vendor directory on real Turso data • password auth + refresh rotation (bcrypt-12, rotation-on-use) • httpOnly session cookie bridge • vendor registration/dashboard/product CRUD w/ moderation queue (**June C-10 auto-approve: fixed**) • fund balance (**June C-08 DATE_TRUNC: fixed**, verified live returning numbers) • vendor ownership checks (**June H-06: fixed**) • importation callback IP-whitelisted • PayHero STK initiation chain works • API security headers excellent • timing-safe webhook compare • zero 500s across all 31 live routes probed • auth-gating correct everywhere live.

---

## Recommended sequence for the polish + harden phase

1. **Decide the architecture** (below) — everything else depends on it
2. **Security hardening**: seal the 5 leak/takeover vectors, web security headers, fix sanitizer, rate-limit server actions
3. **Money-path correctness**: cron double-pay, cancel-race, signature handling, stock decrement, escrow release set-at-payment + transactional, refund field
4. **De-Solera pass**: legal pages rewritten for ADDPlus+, contact form with a real endpoint, brand sweep of every leftover string/key/widget
5. **UX bug sweep**: the HIGH web list, then mediums/lows
6. **Tests + CI + docs**: seed a test suite for auth/payments/escrow, fix workflows, regenerate the forensic README so docs stop lying

Do not change getFundBalance (it already only aggregates 'profit_share_contribution').

3. src/services/mpesaService.ts — validateWebhookSignature(): Safaricom Daraja sends NO signature header on real callbacks, so requiring one permanently blocks production payments. Replace the body with an honest implementation: log the warning if signature absent, then `return true;` unconditionally, with a comment: 'Daraja STK/B2C callbacks carry no signature; authenticity is enforced by the Safaricom IP whitelist checked in routes/payments.ts and importation route. 4. src/routes/uploads.ts — GET /files/:folder/:filename path traversal: before path.join, validate both params against /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/ and reject values containing '..' ; then build with path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'uploads', folder, filename) and verify the resolved path startsWith(path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'uploads')) else 404. 5. src/services/authService.ts — setupPassword() brute-force hardening: add module-level in-memory rate limit (works without Redis): `const setupAttempts = new Map<string, { count: number; resetAt: number }>();` keyed by cleanPhone; allow max 3 attempts per phone per hour (sliding window via resetAt); on exceed throw AppError('Too many attempts. 6. src/services/authService.ts — requestPasswordReset(): anti-enumeration: return the SAME shape for both branches: `{ message: generic.message }`. Remove `emailSent` from the success branch entirely (keep console.error logging of send failures).

Validate each item.quantity is an integer >= 1 up front (throw 400). Keep notifications outside the transaction. Remove the now-dead top-level itemsWithDetails Promise.all duplication (do the price/subtotal computation inside the tx loop).

8. src/services/paymentConfirmationService.ts — confirmOrderPayment(): inside the existing $transaction, after escrow entries are created for each item, also update the order item: `tx.orderItem.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { auto_release_at: in14Days, expected_delivery_at: in14Days } })` where in14Days = new Date(Date.now() + 14*24*3600*1000), computed once before the loop — ONLY set these if you can do it without breaking existing behavior; set them unconditionally (items have null values at this point).

9. Keep openDispute unchanged.

11. Draft leak: src/routes/products.ts public GET '/' — delete `include_drafts: req.query.include_drafts === 'true'` and `status: req.query.status` from filters (public catalog must never see drafts). Same for src/routes/vendors.ts GET '/:id/products' (it doesn't pass include_drafts — verify and leave). Ensure GET '/vendor/me' keeps include_drafts true (authenticated).

12. src/middleware/security.ts — sanitizer corrupts legitimate content (blocks '&' in 'B&B', strips apostrophes/quotes, blocks '--'): 
   - SQL_INJECTION_PATTERNS: reduce to [/(\bUNION\b.*\bSELECT\b)/i, /(\bSLEEP\s*\()/i, /(\bBENCHMARK\s*\()/i]
   - XSS_PATTERNS: keep as-is
   - COMMAND_INJECTION_PATTERNS: empty array (comment: removed — matched legitimate ampersands/quotes)
   - sanitizeString(): remove the quote-stripping replace and the `<>`-stripping replace; keep .trim() and raise substring cap to 2000.
   - validateInput(): stop mutating req.body/req.query (delete both sanitizeObject assignments; detection-only middleware now). Comment why: Prisma parameterizes queries; React escapes output; destructive sanitization corrupted legitimate business names.

13. External call timeouts: add `timeout: 15000` as third arg/config to every axios call in src/services/mpesaService.ts (4 calls) and src/services/smsService.ts (1 call); in src/services/payheroService.ts add `, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) }` hmm fetch signature: fetch(url, { method, headers, body, signal }) — merge signal into both existing option objects; same for the GET in getTransactionStatus; in src/services/emailService.ts add signal to both fetches.

14. src/jobs/crons.ts compliance scoring double-fine guard: before creating the FineLedger row inside the daily job, check `const existingFine = await prisma.fineLedger.findFirst({ where: { vendor_id: vendor.id, rule_violated: 'daily_posting_requirement', created_at: { gte: today } } });` and skip fineLedger.create + fine_balance increment + collectiveFund fine_revenue entry if it exists (still upsert the ComplianceLog).

input.description: Rescue mobile app core
input.prompt:
You are fixing the ADDPlus+ mobile app (React Native + Expo SDK 50) at /home/pop-os/addplus/apps/mobile so it can actually function against production. Backend contract: POST /v1/auth/login expects `{ identifier, password }` (identifier = phone or email); base URL must be https://addplus-api.onrender.com/v1; access tokens expire in 15min, refresh via POST /v1/auth/token/refresh {refreshToken} → { accessToken, refreshToken }; error shape { success:false, error }. Read every file before editing. Do NOT commit. Match existing code style.

FIXES:

1. src/lib/api.ts — (a) default/fallback BASE_URL → 'https://addplus-api.onrender.com/v1'. (b) authApi.login sends { identifier: phoneOrEmail, password }. (c) Guard the AsyncStorage JSON.parse in the request interceptor with try/catch: on parse failure clear the storage key and continue unauthenticated. (d) Add a response interceptor implementing refresh-on-401: if status 401, request has Authorization header, not already retried, and a refreshToken exists → POST /v1/auth/token/refresh; on success update the auth store's tokens (import useAuthStore.getState().setTokens or equivalent — read the store first and add a setTokens action if missing), retry original request with new token; on refresh failure clear session. Prevent refresh stampede with a single in-flight promise shared by concurrent 401s.

2. src/screens/CartScreen.tsx — remove the fail-open catch (~lines 69-73) that fabricates ORD-* ids and shows success. On any checkout/API error: keep the cart intact, stay on current step, Alert.alert('Checkout failed', err?.response?.data?.error || 'Something went wrong. Please try again.').

3. Kill mock-data-as-real fallbacks — read src/lib/mockData.ts first:
   - MarketplaceScreen.tsx: fix the `if (fetched.length === 0) throw new Error('empty')` bug (an empty page is a normal end-of-list, not an error). On genuine fetch error: set an error state with a Retry button — NEVER append/replace with mock products.
   - HomeScreen.tsx: on API failure show section-level empty/retry states instead of mock trending/vendors/discover.
   - OrdersScreen.tsx: empty state 'No orders yet' + CTA to browse marketplace instead of MOCK_ORDERS; error state instead of mock fallback.
   - VendorDashboardScreen.tsx: error state with Retry instead of fabricated earnings/compliance/orders.
4. src/store/useAuthStore.ts — extend the AuthUser type with optional vendor_profile_id?: string so the VendorDashboardScreen cast goes away (keep the runtime gate).

5. src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx — Saved Items / Buyer Protection / Help & Support rows: render as disabled (no onPress, muted color, small 'Coming soon' right-label) instead of dead handlers.

6. src/screens/ProductDetailScreen.tsx — wishlist heart currently fires a lying Alert: remove the heart button entirely (no wishlist system exists) OR render it visually disabled with opacity 0.4 and no handler; choose whichever fits surrounding code better.

7. Cart navigation dead-ends: read App.tsx navigator structure. From ProductDetailScreen and VendorStoreScreen (registered in root Stack), navigation.navigate('Cart') fails because Cart lives in the tab navigator. Fix with nested navigate: navigation.navigate(<MainTabName>, { screen: <CartRouteName> }) using the ACTUAL registered names.

8. src/App.tsx — the header bell navigates to Cart wearing the cart badge (lying affordance): remove the bell button from HomeScreen header instead (edit src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx accordingly). Also wrap registerForPushNotificationsAsync().catch(() => {}) so no unhandled rejection, and only call registerPushToken AFTER successful login AND wrap in .catch(() => {}) (already done — verify).

9. Assets: create apps/mobile/assets/ directory with valid PNGs generated via Python PIL (available on system): icon.png 1024x1024 (solid #22C55E background, white bold '+' centered ~60% size, font DejaVu-Sans-Bold), adaptive-icon.png 1024x1024 (same motif on transparent-capable white background), splash.png 1242x2436 (white background, centered green 'ADDPlus+' wordmark text ~120px), favicon.png 48x48 (green bg white '+'). Verify files exist and are non-trivial size afterwards.

10. CI/deps: run `cd /home/pop-os/addplus/apps/mobile && npm install --package-lock-only --legacy-peer-deps` to generate package-lock.json. Add "@expo/vector-icons" to dependencies at the version Expo SDK 50 expects (check node_modules/@expo/vector-icons/package.json version after root install; if absent use "^14.0.0"). Create a minimal tsconfig.json extending "expo/tsconfig.base" with strict false, jsx react-native. In eas.json remove the invalid gradleCommand line from the development profile (managed workflow has no android/ dir). Leave eas projectId as-is but add "// TODO: run eas init to get real project ID" comment ABOVE the line in app.json (JSON has no comments — instead note it in your final report; make NO app.json edit for this).

11. app.json — update the extra.apiUrl value to https://addplus-api.onrender.com/v1.

REPORT: numbered per-file summary of every change (one line each), assets verification (ls -la output), lockfile confirmation, and anything you could not complete with reason.

'use client'

import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
import { Navbar } from '@/components/navbar'

const HIDE_NAVBAR_PREFIXES = [
  '/admin',
  '/vendor',
  '/account',
  '/login',
  '/dashboard',
  '/products',
  '/orders',
  '/earnings',
  '/compliance',
  '/store',
  '/vendors',
  '/disputes',
  '/fund',
  '/insights',
  '/settings',
  '/messages',
  '/onboarding',
  '/signup',
  '/verify-email',
]

export function ConditionalChrome({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const hideNavbar = HIDE_NAVBAR_PREFIXES.some(
    (p) => pathname === p || pathname.startsWith(`${p}/`)
  )

  return (
    <>
      {!hideNavbar && <Navbar />}
      <main
        className={
          hideNavbar
            ? ''
            : 'marketplace-site min-h-screen bg-[var(--surface-page)] text-[var(--text-primary)]'
        }
      >
        {children}
      </main>
    </>
  )
}

# ADDPlus+ — Nairobi's Collective SME Marketplace

> One M-Pesa payment. Multiple vendors. Funds held until you say so.

ADDPlus+ is a multi-vendor marketplace built specifically for Nairobi's informal and semi-formal SME ecosystem — fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, and fragrance — unified under one roof with escrow-backed payments, compliance scoring, and a collective advancement fund.

A full-stack audit (web, API, mobile, live) was completed 2026-08-25. Findings supersede the June sections below where they conflict:

# 1. WHAT ADDPLUS+ IS

ADDPlus+ began around the idea of building a structured platform for commerce and transactions involving vendors and customers.

It has progressively evolved beyond the idea of a simple online marketplace.

The broad direction of ADDPlus+ is now best understood as an ecosystem around:

* Commerce
* Merchants
* Customers
* Products
* Services
* Errands
* Logistics
* Delivery
* Supply/procurement
* Operational coordination
* Trust
* Potential financial infrastructure

The long-term strategic framing that emerged was:

> **ADDPlus+ is potentially evolving into a Commerce + Fulfillment + Errands Ecosystem.**

Another framing used during strategic discussions was:

> **A Commerce Operating System for African businesses and communities.**

However, this should not be interpreted as meaning all of those verticals must be built now.

A major principle is:

> **Do not try to build the entire ecosystem at once. Build in layers and validate operational concepts before engineering large systems around them.**

---

# 2. CORE PRODUCT EVOLUTION

## Original/core direction

The earlier direction centered around a marketplace structure:

```text
Customers
    ↕
ADDPlus+ Platform
    ↕
Vendors
```

The marketplace needed infrastructure for:

* Product discovery
* Vendors
* Vendor storefronts
* Products
* Shopping
* Cart
* Checkout
* Orders
* Payments
* Trust/governance

This led to the realization that vendors themselves needed an operating interface rather than simply being passive sellers.

That introduced the next major layer:

> **MerchantOS / Vendor Operating System**

---

# 3. THE MERCHANTOS / VENDOR DASHBOARD DIRECTION

One of the major next steps identified for ADDPlus+ was the introduction of an administrative interface/dashboard for respective parties and roles.

The immediate concern was specifically that:

> Vendors should be able to add, remove, manage products and manage other information related to their businesses.

The direction was therefore to move away from a marketplace where product/vendor data is manually controlled and toward a role-based system where relevant users manage their own data.

The vendor/admin system was envisioned around:

* Authentication
* Role-based access control
* Vendor dashboards
* Product management
* Inventory
* Orders
* Vendor/store information
* Analytics
* Activity logs
* Platform administration and governance

The technical direction discussed for this work was:

* Next.js
* Turso / libSQL database
* Database management via Turso CLI
* A suitable ORM/database abstraction layer
* Role-based authentication and authorization
* Deployment through Vercel
* Development using AI-assisted/vibe-coding workflows, particularly Cursor at that stage

A key implementation principle was:

> **Do not build fake dashboards that only look functional. Connect dashboards to real backend/database systems wherever practical.**

# 4. ROLE-BASED ARCHITECTURE

The original role model was roughly:

```text
CUSTOMER
VENDOR
ADMIN
```

As the product expanded conceptually, the role system was considered capable of growing toward:

```text
CUSTOMER
VENDOR
ADMIN
OPERATIONS
RUNNER
PARTNER
```

Potential future roles included:

```text
FINANCE
SUPER_ADMIN
```

These are not necessarily all implemented.

The conceptual responsibility of each role is as follows.

## CUSTOMER

The person using ADDPlus+ to:

* Discover products
* Browse vendors
* Purchase products
* Request relevant services
* Track orders
* Potentially request errands or deliveries
* Manage their account

## VENDOR

A merchant/business using ADDPlus+ to:

* Manage store information
* Add products
* Edit products
* Remove/archive products
* Manage stock/inventory
* Receive/manage orders
* Potentially manage promotions
* View business activity
* View analytics

## ADMIN

The platform governance role responsible for:

* Managing users
* Managing/approving vendors
* Monitoring products
* Moderation
* Orders oversight
* Reports
* Disputes
* Audit logs
* Platform configuration
* Overall platform health

## OPERATIONS

A future operational role responsible for coordinating real-world activity such as:

* Pending requests
* Dispatch
* Assignment
* Delivery operations
* Task fulfillment
* Operational monitoring

## RUNNER

A future role for people carrying out physical tasks.

Possible capabilities:

* View assigned tasks
* Accept/manage assignments
* Complete errands
* Carry out deliveries
* Track completed work
* View earnings
* Manage availability
* Receive ratings

## PARTNER

Potentially relevant because ADDPlus+ is not purely a one-person project. Partners may participate in business operations, strategic initiatives, or future ecosystem verticals.

# 17. THE MOST IMPORTANT STRATEGIC PRINCIPLE

The biggest danger identified was trying to build everything at once.

ADDPlus+ potentially touches:

* Marketplace technology
* Merchant software
* Logistics
* Human operations
* Procurement
* Payments
* Services
* Trust infrastructure

This can become extremely complex.

Therefore:

> **Build the digital infrastructure in focused layers.**

And:

> **Validate operational services manually before building complex software for them.**

The suggested validation approach for new operational services was to initially use simple/manual channels such as:

* WhatsApp
* Calls
* Forms
* Direct coordination

The purpose is to learn:

* Is there demand?
* How often do requests occur?
* What are people actually requesting?
* How should pricing work?
* What are the operational bottlenecks?
* What trust/safety problems arise?
* Does the model generate enough margin?

Only after learning from real operations should heavy automation be considered.

# 48. DEVELOPMENT PHILOSOPHY

The following principles have consistently emerged around ADDPlus+.

## Principle 1 — Build real systems

Avoid dashboards that are purely visual mockups when the intention is for them to be functional.

Use real:

* Database records
* Authentication
* Authorization
* Relationships
* State
* APIs/server actions

where the feature is supposed to be real.

---

## Principle 2 — Build in layers

Do not attempt to simultaneously build:

* Marketplace
* Full MerchantOS
* Logistics
* Runner infrastructure
* Procurement
* Services marketplace
* Financial infrastructure

The correct approach is staged.

---

## Principle 3 — Validate before overengineering

For highly operational services like errands and logistics:

```text
Manual Validation
        ↓
Real Demand
        ↓
Operational Learning
        ↓
Repeatable Workflow
        ↓
Software Support
        ↓
Automation/Scaling
```

---

## Principle 4 — Separate strategic modules

Do not force every ADDPlus+ capability into one monolithic feature.

Conceptually:

```text
ADDPlus+
│
├── Marketplace
├── Merchant Tools
├── Governance
├── Operations
└── Future Service Modules
```

A modular architecture is preferable.

---

## Principle 5 — Real African commerce realities matter

The product should not blindly imitate Western e-commerce systems.

Relevant realities may include:

* Informal merchants
* Shared businesses
* Physical stalls
* Hybrid online/offline selling
* WhatsApp commerce
* Commission-based sales
* Informal logistics
* Trust concerns
* Local payment behavior
* Small-business inventory constraints

This does not mean every informal workflow must be supported immediately.

It means product decisions should remain grounded in the market.

## PART 1: PROJECT OVERVIEW

### 1.1 What Is ADDPlus+?

ADDPlus+ is a multi-vendor SME collective marketplace built for Nairobi's informal and semi-formal business ecosystem — fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, and fragrance — unified under one digital roof with escrow-backed payments, compliance scoring, and a collective advancement fund.

**Core Thesis:**
- One cart, many vendors — customer pays once via M-Pesa
- Escrow — funds held until buyer confirms delivery (or auto-release after timeout)
- 10% transaction levy — split 5% to collective advancement fund + 5% to platform profit share
- Compliance scoring — vendors earn visibility through daily posts and referral activity

### 1.2 The Vision (Newton Murimi Kiura)

> *"It takes ages to build an empire alone but it takes days to build it collectively. The customer who buys a dress might need a necklace, cake, catering, shoes, a watch, makeup, a hairdresser, and fragrance. ADDPlus+ is the one platform where all of that exists. As you ADD, another will Plus and the other will + the glow. The party will be complete."*

### 1.3 Core Beliefs

| Belief | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Collective over Competition | Businesses co-existing on one platform multiply each other's revenue |
| Structure before Profit | Long-term survival is built on discipline, consistency, connectivity |
| Everyone Has Something to ADD | No business is too small |
| Trust is Commerce | Escrow and accountability ARE the product's trust engine |
| Simplicity Earns Loyalty | If a user needs to think for more than 3 seconds, the design has failed |

## PART 11: BUSINESS MODEL

### 11.1 Revenue Model

| Source | Rate | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| **Transaction Levy** | 10% per sale | 5% → Collective Advancement Fund, 5% → Profit-Share Pool |
| **Vendor Net** | 90% of sale | Held in escrow until delivery confirmation |
| **Errands (future)** | Flat fee | Runner payout + platform margin |

### 11.2 Compliance Rules

| Rule | Mon-Fri | Sat-Sun |
|------|---------|---------|
| Min daily posts | 1 product post/day | No minimum |
| Max daily posts | 3 posts/day | 3 posts/day |
| Post types allowed | Product posts | Profile/business only |
| Referral shares | 3 per week | 3 per week |

### 11.3 Compliance Score Formula (40/40/20)

- **Post compliance (40%):** min(posts made / posts_required, 1.0) × 40
- **Referral compliance (40%):** min(referrals made / 3, 1.0) × 40
- **Profile post compliance (20%):** (profile_post_made ? 1 : 0) × 20

### 11.4 Escrow Flow

1. Customer pays via M-Pesa STK Push
2. Funds held in escrow (5%+5% levy deducted)
3. Vendor dispatches order
4. Customer confirms delivery OR auto-release after timeout
5. Escrow released to vendor via B2C

## WHAT ADDPLUS+ IS

ADDPlus+ is a multi-vendor marketplace where independent Nairobi businesses co-exist under one digital roof. Customers shop across multiple vendors and pay **once with M-Pesa**. Funds are held in escrow until the customer confirms delivery.

**Core thesis:**
- One cart, many vendors — customer pays once via M-Pesa
- Escrow — funds held until buyer confirms delivery (or 48h auto-release after dispatch)
- 10% transaction levy per sale: 5% → Collective Advancement Fund, 5% → Profit-Share Pool
- Compliance scoring — vendors earn visibility via daily posting + referral activity (40/40/20 formula)
- Collective grants — 2 vendors/month, up to KES 20,000 each, from the fund

**Newton's founding vision:** "It takes ages to build an empire alone but days to build it collectively. The customer who buys a dress might need a necklace, cake, catering, shoes, a watch, makeup, a hairdresser, and fragrance. ADDPlus+ is the one platform where all of that exists."

## AUTHENTICATION FLOW

```
POST /v1/auth/login { phone, password }
  → normalize phone to 254XXXXXXXXX
  → bcrypt.compare against User.password_hash
  → if no hash and role admin/vendor → { needsPasswordSetup: true }
  → JWT access (HS256, 15m) + refresh token (UUID, 7d in DB)
  → response includes vendor_profile_id when VendorProfile exists

POST /v1/auth/password/setup { phone, password }
  → bcrypt hash → User.password_hash (first-time setup)

Protected routes → Bearer JWT
  → Redis blacklist check (optional — if Redis configured)
  → Redis user cache (5m) or DB fallback
  → authorize('vendor', 'admin') on vendor self-service routes

Session cookies set via Next.js API route /api/auth/session
  → httpOnly cookies: access_token, refresh_token, user_role
  → demo-token-* rejected by middleware
```

OTP flow: `ENABLE_OTP_AUTH=false` on Render — all OTP routes return 503.

## BUSINESS LOGIC

### Escrow & Levy Flow

On successful STK callback:
1. Order status → `confirmed`
2. Per order item: `EscrowLedger` created with status `held`
3. 5% of subtotal → `CollectiveFund` as `advancement_contribution`
4. 5% of subtotal → `CollectiveFund` as `profit_share_contribution`
5. 90% net held for vendor

On delivery confirm OR cron auto-release:
1. Deduct vendor's `fine_balance` from net payout
2. Initiate B2C to vendor `mpesa_number` if net ≥ KES 500
3. Escrow status → `released`

**Gap:** `auto_release_at` is set when vendor marks `dispatched` (+48h). NOT set at payment. If vendor never dispatches, cron never fires and escrow stays held forever.

### Compliance Scoring (40/40/20)

```
weekly_score = (posts_made/posts_required × 0.40)
             + (referrals_shared/3 × 0.40)
             + (profile_post_made ? 1 : 0 × 0.20)
             × 100
```

Rolling 7-day average stored on `VendorProfile.compliance_score`.

Posting rules:
- Mon–Fri: min 1 product post/day, max 3/day
- Weekends: profile posts only, max 3
- Referral shares: 3/week minimum

Thresholds:
- ≥ 75%: eligible for profit share + grant application
- 60–74%: profit share only
- 40–59%: warning issued
- < 40%: KES 200 fine + possible posting suspension

### Collective Fund

- Grant: 2 vendors/month, up to KES 20,000
- Grants > KES 10,000 require equity stake (5–10%)
- Eligibility: compliance ≥ 75%, zero fine balance
- Profit-share: distributed weekly (Monday 06:00) to compliant vendors proportional to compliance score

input.command:
cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, urllib.request, urllib.parse

KEY = "[REDACTED-GOOGLE-API-KEY-by-backup]"
QUERIES = [
 ("kenya-ecom", "Kenya e-commerce marketplace startups"),
 ("jumia-lesson", "Jumia Africa e-commerce failure lessons"),
 ("mpesa-biz", "M-Pesa business commerce Kenya"),
 ("informal-sme", "informal economy digitization Africa SMEs"),
 ("unit-econ", "marketplace startup take rate unit economics"),
 ("trust-escrow", "trust escrow online marketplace Africa"),
 ("sendy", "Sendy Kenya logistics startup shutdown"),
 ("whatsapp-comm", "WhatsApp social commerce Africa sellers"),
 ("nairobi-eco", "Nairobi startup ecosystem funding"),
 ("dpa", "Kenya Data Protection Act compliance startups"),
]
def get(url):
    try:
        return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=20))
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}

out = []
for tag, q in QUERIES:
    s = get(f"https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/search?part=snippet&maxResults=5&type=video&order=relevance&publishedAfter=2022-01-01T00:00:00Z&q={urllib.parse.quote(q)}&key={KEY}")
    items = s.get("items", [])
    ids = [i["id"]["videoId"] for i in items if i.get("id",{}).get("videoId")]
    stats = {}
    if ids:
        v = get(f"https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/videos?part=statistics,contentDetails&id={','.join(ids)}&key={KEY}")
        stats = {x["id"]: x["statistics"] for x in v.get("items", [])}
    out.append(f"\n### {tag} — {q}")
    for i in items:
        vid = i.get("id",{}).get("videoId","?")
        sn = i["snippet"]
        st = stats.get(vid, {})
        views = st.get("viewCount","?")
        desc = sn["description"].replace("\n"," ")[:160]
        out.append(f"- [{sn['channelTitle']}|{views}v|{sn['publishedAt'][:10]}] {sn['title']}\n  {desc}")
open("/tmp/yt_research.txt","w").write("\n".join(out))
print("\n".join(out)[:400])
print("...written /tmp/yt_research.txt", len("\n".join(out)), "chars")
EOF
