Research done. Here's the full synthesis — the three briefs, the codebase truth from our audit, and what the market evidence actually says.

---

# What ADDPlus+ really is (the honest map)

## 1. How we arrived here — diagnosed

Your three briefing documents describe **three different companies**:

| Brief | Says ADDPlus+ is | Emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | "Commerce + Fulfillment + Errands Ecosystem / Commerce OS for Africa" | Ambition |
| v2 | SME collective marketplace — escrow, 10% levy, compliance scoring, collective fund | Mechanism |
| v3 | Same + ZawadiRuns errands integration, partner structure (Newton CEO / you CTO / Zawadi ops) | People |

Every brief repeats the same golden rule: *"Build in layers. Validate operational services manually before engineering around them."* **And the codebase violates it spectacularly.** We built Phase-4 financial infrastructure — escrow ledger, levy splitting, profit-share cron, collective fund grants, compliance fines, importation deposits — while M-Pesa live sits at 12% and **zero real orders have ever flowed through**. That's the "how did we arrive here": we engineered ahead of demand. The audit found the machinery excellent and idle.

## 2. What the YouTube evidence screams

The research pulled a consistent story:

- **The marketplace/logistics graveyard is real.** Jumia raised $600M+, rang the NYSE bell, "has not made a single dollar in profits ever." Sendy raised **$80M and shut down in 2023** — in Nairobi, your city, your exact adjacency. KBC's trade-ministry piece: *"Kenya's e-commerce market remains low due to high delivery costs."*
- **Where Kenyan commerce is actually growing: conversation.** Chpter is scaling across Africa on WhatsApp commerce; the highest-view business content is "how to sell on WhatsApp" (100K–845K views). Your own market insight from Zawadi — shared stalls, commission selling, hybrid physical/digital — says vendors already have channels. They don't need another destination website.
- **Funding has consolidated** — "4 companies took 70% of Kenya's tech funding." Nobody funds pre-traction marketplaces anymore.
- **Compliance infrastructure exists and is active** — ODPC/DPA practitioners, fintech licensing guidance. Escrow-held customer funds is a **CBK payment-service-provider question**, not just a feature.

## 3. My honest take

ADDPlus+'s genuinely differentiated idea is **not the marketplace** — Jumia/Kilimall own that ground and bled out on it. It's the **trust layer**: *escrow so strangers can transact + a collective fund so vendors co-own the upside*. Newton's quote is the best positioning sentence in all three briefs. But two assumptions are unvalidated and heavy:

1. **The 10% levy.** A vendor selling on WhatsApp pays 0%. You're asking for 10% — that's only rational if escrow + fund membership visibly earns it. Market take-rates evolve slowly (the unit-economics material is blunt about this). Test 5%. Test flat fees. Let vendors feel the fund.
2. **Daily posting compliance.** Asking an overloaded SME to post daily to keep visibility is a tax on their scarcest resource. It may drive engagement or it may be the reason vendors churn. Only real vendors can answer.

And the strategic irony: **your distribution channel is fighting your market.** The market lives on WhatsApp; ADDPlus+ is a destination site. The winning shape is probably *WhatsApp-first commerce with ADDPlus+ escrow rails* — shareable product cards that open an escrowed checkout link — meeting sellers where they already sell (this is exactly what Chpter proved works).

## 4. What I'd do next (validation before anything)

1. **Get 20 real transactions.** Not users — *paid orders*, manually recruited from Newton's and Zawadi's actual networks. Measure: STK completion rate, buyer trust in escrow, vendor reaction to the levy, delivery friction.
2. **Freeze the governance machinery** (profit-share payouts, fines, importation) until there's a vendor base it governs. Dead rules breed dead code — we just cleaned out a whole dead platform.
3. **One lawyer conversation**: ODPC data-controller registration (cheap, required) + whether escrow-holding needs PSP licensing. Before scale, not after.
4. **Resolve the partnership paper** (the equity draft). Three founders aligned beat any feature roadmap — and investors will ask first.
5. Then decide the errands layer with ZawadiRuns data — manual pilot, per your own Phase-3 principle.

---

My one-sentence version: **ADDPlus+ is a beautifully engineered trust thesis that has never touched a customer — and the fastest way to find out if it's a company is 20 real paid orders, not more software.**

Your move — push back anywhere. If the direction lands, I can turn this into a lean validation playbook (recruitment scripts, measurement sheet, levy A/B design, WhatsApp card prototype spec) as the next concrete work item.

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it — a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits — link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=…&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* — most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token — a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject — or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name — a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word — a greeting, a category, a page-type label — the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

input.content:
ADDPlus+ · Validation Sprint · Aug–Sep 2026

First Orders
Playbook

Twenty real paid orders in thirty days — run manually, measured honestly, no new software. The goal isn't growth. It's finding out whether the machine we built deserves customers.

20paid orders
10vendors recruited
30days
0new features

Why this exists

We built escrow, levies, compliance scoring, and a collective fund before a single real transaction flowed through. The audit proved the machinery works; nothing has proven anyone wants it. Jumia never turned a profit on $600M raised; Sendy burned $80M and shut down two kilometres from our market. The difference between us and them can't be more features — it has to be contact with reality.

The rule of this sprint: everything is tested by hand first. WhatsApp, calls, the existing site, one shared spreadsheet. Software freezes until the data says otherwise.

The three bets

H1 — Buyers will pay into escrow

A customer who found a vendor through a WhatsApp link will complete an M-Pesa STK payment to a platform they've never used, trusting money they can't see until delivery.

H2 — Vendors will accept the levy

A vendor selling free on WhatsApp will give up a share of each sale for escrow protection and fund membership — and tell us their honest breaking point.

H3 — One person can run dispatch

Zawadi can coordinate vendor → buyer delivery for twenty orders without the process collapsing into phone-tag chaos.

If all three hold, ADDPlus+ has a business shape. If any fails, we just learned what to build next — or what not to.

Recruiting vendors

Ten sellers from Newton's and Zawadi's real networks. Criteria: actively selling, holds stock, reachable by phone, sells anything in our categories (fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, fragrance). Mix stalls and Instagram/WhatsApp sellers deliberately — hybrid sellers are the truest test.

The pitch, word for word

WhatsApp / call script · Newton or Zawadi"Tunaanzisha platform ya kuuzia pamoja — ADDPlus+. Wewe unauza kama kawaida, sisi tunakupa duka mtandaoni na malipo ya M-Pesa yanasimamiwa hadi mteka apokee. Kwa miezi moja tunatoa na wewe tu %5, si %10. Tunataka watu kumi tu kuanzia — uko tayari?"
(We're launching a collective selling platform. You sell as usual; we give you an online storefront and hold M-Pesa payments until your customer receives. For one month we waive it to 5%, not 10%. We're taking ten vendors only.)

The honesty clause

Tell every vendor up front: the standard rate is 10%. After their third order we ask directly whether they'd stay at 10%. Their answer is data point H2 — do not soften the question.

Getting orders

Vendors share product links into their own WhatsApp statuses and groups — the channel where their buyers already live. No ads, no new socials. Each link opens the product page on addplus.vercel.app with checkout and STK payment already live. Two orders per vendor is the target; twenty across ten vendors.

The buyer message vendors send

Vendor → buyer status / DM"Nimeeka bidhaa zangu kwenye ADDPlus+ — lipa kwa M-Pesa salama, pesa inasimamiwa hadi ufike nayo. Angalia hapa: [link]"
(I've listed my goods on ADDPlus+ — pay safely with M-Pesa; funds are held until you receive. See here.)
Pilot promise: any dispute during the pilot gets a full refund, no questions asked, same day. Refunds are the cost of learning; log every one.

Running the loop

PersonOwns dailyExplicitly not doing
NewtonVendor recruitment & relationships; weekly check-in call with each vendorProduct decisions
ZawadiDispatch coordination, buyer support, refunds, the order sheetNew service lines
KenFixing only what breaks payments or blocks an orderAll new features — freeze holds

One shared Google Sheet is the entire system of record. Thirty-minute review every Monday: numbers below, decisions logged, nothing else discussed.

The scorecard

Every order logs one row. These eight columns are the whole experiment:

#FieldWhy it matters
1order_id · date · vendorIdentity
2stk_sent → stk_done?H1 core: did the payment complete? Time between matters too.
3mins_to_payTrust hesitation shows up as delay or abandonment
4delivered_confirmed?Did the buyer confirm receipt (releasing escrow)?
5hrs_vendor_to_dispatchH3: how fast can a human move goods?
6dispute? refund?Trust failures, counted honestly
7levy_reactionVerbatim vendor comment on the fee, after payout
8would_repeat?Asked of buyer post-delivery: yes / no / maybe

Decision gates

Gate A — after 5 orders

SignalThresholdCall
STK completion≥ 60%continue
STK completion< 60%stop & fix payments first

Gate B — after 20 orders

QuestionPassIterateKill signal
Would buyers pay again?≥ 40% yes25–39% — study drop-off< 25%
Vendors staying at 10%?≥ half say yesTest 7.5% / flat KESNobody accepts ≥ 5%
Dispatch within 48h?≥ 80%Add runner support< 50%
Refund rate≤ 10%10–20% — fix vendor quality> 20%

Two kill signals = stop, write the post-mortem, redirect. That is a win too — it costs thirty days instead of eighteen months.

Asking about the levy

After each vendor's third payout — never at signup, always after real money landed:

Levy interview · Newton, verbatim"Umepata malipo yako. Swali moja la kweli: kama ada ingekuwa asilimia kumi badala ya tano, ungeendelea? Na kama hapana — ngapi ndiyo kiwango chako?"
(You've been paid. One honest question: if the fee were ten percent instead of five, would you continue? If not — what's your limit?)

Record the exact percentage they name. Ten answers draw the demand curve no pitch deck can fake.

WhatsApp cards · next build

The only software worth building during the sprint, and only after Gate A passes: a generated preview card per product — image, price, vendor, "Pay via M-Pesa · held until delivered" — sharing to WhatsApp as a rich link that opens the product page. Track share → click → order per card. If buyers convert from a card inside WhatsApp at even half the rate of direct links, distribution stops being a guess.

Compliance, while we're at it

  • Register with the ODPC as a data controller — required under the Data Protection Act, inexpensive, do it this month
  • Book one session with a commercial lawyer: does holding buyer funds in escrow require CBK PSP licensing at pilot scale? Get the answer in writing
  • Draft the one-page partnership paper — equity split, vesting, IP — before revenue makes it harder

The calendar

WeekMilestone
W1Recruit 10 vendors · ODPC filed · sheet live · lawyer booked · first 3 orders
W210 orders cumulative · Gate A review · levy interviews begin
W316 orders · WhatsApp card prototype if Gate A passed · partnership paper drafted
W4Order #20 · Gate B review · go / iterate / stop decision, written and signed off by all three

Built from the August 2026 audit and strategy sessions · Kennedy Muritu, Newton Murimi Kiura, Mercy Zawadi · The machine is ready. This document finds out if anyone wants it.

# ADDPlus+ — Reality Baseline (Drawing Board Document)

**Date:** 2026-08-25 · **Basis:** code trace at HEAD `53ca0a4` + live probes + Aug audit
**Purpose:** separate what we HAVE from what we ASSUME. This is the pre-product drawing board.

---

## A. Verified working (touched by real traffic)

| Capability | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Catalog + vendor storefronts on live Turso | 12 products / 6 categories served publicly |
| Accounts: signup w/ Brevo verification, login, forgot/reset, refresh rotation, httpOnly cookie bridge | Live-tested |
| Vendor portal: register wizard, product CRUD w/ moderation queue, orders, earnings, store settings | Working endpoints + pages |
| Admin console: overview, KYC approve/reject/suspend, orders, disputes list, insights | 13 endpoints live |
| Order creation: atomic stock check + decrement + movement record | Fixed this pass, tsc-verified |
| Security posture: headers both tiers, bcrypt-12, timing-safe webhook compare, rate limits, ownership checks | Verified |

## B. Built but NEVER fired once in production (unproven machinery)

1. **The entire payment loop**: STK initiation exists, but **zero paid orders have ever occurred**. Nothing downstream has ever run against real money.
2. **Callback → confirmation → escrow**: `confirmOrderPayment` (escrow rows, levy splits, status flip) only triggers via PayHero callback proxied through Vercel. Fails closed without `PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET` matching on both Render and the PayHero dashboard. This chain has never been exercised.
3. **Vendor payouts (B2C)**: need *separate* Daraja go-live credentials (initiator name + security credential) beyond STK creds. Almost certainly never configured ⇒ even a "released" escrow pays nobody.
4. **All three crons** (escrow auto-release, compliance scoring, profit-share): node-cron runs only while the Render free-tier instance is awake; it sleeps after ~15 min idle ⇒ jobs fire late or never until the next request wakes the box.
5. Importation deposits, collective-fund grants/disbursement, compliance fines — governance machinery governing zero vendors.

## C. Assumed-but-false (the payments story vs reality)

| We say | Actually |
|---|---|
| "Funds held until you say so" | There is **no custody/trust account**. Money lands in the platform's own PayHero/Daraja settlement balance. "Escrow" is a database row, not segregation of funds. |
| One M-Pesa payment splits to vendors | Customer pays the platform once; vendors are owed IOUs in a ledger until B2C exists. Today the platform would hold **all** money indefinitely. |
| COD checkout | UI-complete; backend has **no state for it** — COD orders stay `pending_payment` forever, invisible as fulfillable. Fires no payment by design, so nothing ever advances them. |
| Dispute → refund | Resolution flips statuses; **no rail moves money back to any buyer**. Refunds exist as a column. |
| Escrow auto-release protects buyers | Depends on a cron on a server that's usually asleep. |
| Cart totals are authoritative | Shipping/pickup/promo amounts ride in `delivery_address` JSON as notes; server prices orders from catalog only — client-shown totals can drift from charged totals. |
| Levy = 10% (5+5) | Computed on item subtotals inside the callback; delivery/KES-150 service fee bypasses levy entirely — unaudited revenue leak. |

## D. What was overlooked entirely

- **No ops surface**: nothing answers "which orders must be dispatched today?" across paid/COD states.
- **No reconciliation view**: platform-to-vendor payables, fund balance vs payouts owed — computable but never assembled.
- **Returns/restock**: stock decrements exist; nothing reverses it (disputes, refunds, cancellations).
- **Delivery is fiction**: pickup stations and boda options are mock arrays; no rider, no tracking events, no cost model.
- **Reviews**: schema exists, no submission route, no UI write path.
- **SMS**: Kenya is an SMS market; not one transactional SMS is wired (Brevo SMTP only).
- **No staging**: every experiment hits `addplus-db` production; seed and real data coexist (GMV dashboards already count seed rows).
- **Mobile push**: tokens collected, Expo credentials missing ⇒ silently dead.

## E. Honest one-line product definition (today)

> ADDPlus+ is a working marketplace front door (catalog, accounts, vendor tools) wrapped around a payment-and-escrow state machine that has never completed a single cycle with real money.

## F. Consequence for the validation sprint

Gate A isn't "does STK convert" — it is **first-ever commissioning of the money loop**. Practical requirements added to the playbook:

1. Ken on standby during every first STK attempt; log callback arrival vs timeout.
2. Before vendor #1: verify in PayHero dashboard that the callback URL + secret are actually saved; send a manual test charge of KES 1 end-to-end.
3. Written manual fallback: if STK fails in the field, vendor collects on personal till and Zawadi logs the order manually — the pilot measures demand even when rails fail.
4. COD: either remove from checkout for the pilot, or add the missing `cod_pending` state + vendor-visible flag first (small fix, do before W1).
5. Decide custody story before scale: whose paybill, whose float, PSP question for the lawyer.

## Rules of the sprint
1. Everything manual first: WhatsApp, calls, the existing site, one Google Sheet.

4. Standard rate is 10% and we say so; pilot runs at 5%.

From Newton's + Zawadi's real networks. Actively selling, holds stock, phone-reachable; mix stall traders and Instagram/WhatsApp sellers.

**Pitch (verbatim):**
> "Tunaanzisha platform ya kuuzia pamoja — ADDPlus+. Wewe unauza kama kawaida, sisi tunakupa duka mtandaoni na malipo ya M-Pesa yanasimamiwa hadi mteka apokee. Kwa miezi moja tunatoa na wewe tu %5, si %10. Tunataka watu kumi tu kuanzia — uko tayari?"

| Person | Owns daily | Not doing |
|---|---|---|
| Newton | Vendor recruitment + weekly check-ins | Product decisions |
| Zawadi | Dispatch coordination, buyer support, refunds, the sheet | New service lines |
| Ken | Fixes blocking orders/payments only | All new features |

- [ ] PayHero dashboard: callback URL + secret verified saved; matches Render env
- [ ] One manual KES 1 end-to-end test charge completed and confirmed

- [ ] Manual fallback documented: STK fails → personal till → log manually

## Levy interview (after 3rd payout — never at signup)
> "Umepata malipo yako. Swali moja la kweli: kama ada ingekuwa asilimia kumi badala ya tano, ungeendelea? Na kama hapana — ngapi ndiyo kiwango chako?"

Record the exact percentage named.

## Decision gates
**Gate A — after 5 orders:** STK completion ≥60% → continue · <60% → stop & fix payments first

**Gate B — after 20 orders:**
| Question | Pass | Iterate | Kill |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buyers would repeat? | ≥40% yes | 25–39% | <25% |
| Vendors stay at 10%? | ≥ half | test 7.5%/flat | none accept ≥5% |
| Dispatch ≤48h | ≥80% | add runner help | <50% |
| Refund rate | ≤10% | 10–20% | >20% |

Two kill signals = stop, write post-mortem, redirect. That's a 30-day lesson, not an 18-month burn.

- **W1** — recruit 10 · pre-flight checklist done · first 3 orders · ODPC filed
- **W2** — 10 cumulative · Gate A · levy interviews begin
- **W3** — 16 · WhatsApp share-card prototype only if Gate A passed · partnership paper drafted
- **W4** — order #20 · Gate B · go/iterate/stop decision signed by all three

## Monday ritual
30 minutes. Numbers from the sheet. Decisions logged. Nothing else discussed.

You are re-authenticating the ADDPlus+ website at /home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web (Next.js 15, Tailwind, CSS-var theming). Mission from the owner: make the live site reflect the product vision TO THE CORE, claim ONLY what verifiably works, remove ALL generic/fake/dev-leftover content, and fix bugs across all states (loading/error/empty, light/dark). Do not commit. Run `cd /home/pop-os/addplus/apps/web && npm run build 2>&1 | tail -8` at the end and iterate until green.

## THE VISION (use this voice everywhere)
ADDPlus+ = Nairobi's collective SME marketplace. Founding thesis (Newton Murimi Kiura): "It takes ages to build an empire alone but days to build it collectively. The customer who buys a dress might need a necklace, cake, catering, shoes, a watch, makeup, a hairdresser, and fragrance. As you ADD, another will Plus." Tagline: "One M-Pesa payment. Multiple vendors. Funds held until you say so." Categories: fashion, food, beauty, accessories, catering, fragrance. Value pillars: (1) Collective over competition — vendors multiply each other's revenue; (2) Escrow trust — M-Pesa payment held until buyer confirms delivery; (3) Collective Advancement Fund — 5% of every sale funds vendor grants (the other 5% runs the platform). Audience: informal/semi-formal Nairobi sellers AND their buyers. Voice: warm, Kenyan, plain-spoken, confident — never Silicon Valley SaaS-speak ("empower", "seamless", "revolutionize", "unlock", "supercharge" are banned words).

## TRUTH RULES (hard)
Read /home/pop-os/addplus/docs/REALITY_BASELINE.md first. Claims allowed: multi-vendor cart w/ single M-Pesa payment; payment held until delivery confirmed; vendor storefronts + dashboards; collective fund exists (5% levy). Claims FORBIDDEN: user/vendor counts, testimonials, ratings claims, "trusted by thousands", COD promises (COD disabled), review promises (no real reviews yet), delivery guarantees/timelines (logistics not built), flash sales (feature removed). Where the old copy promised these, rewrite honestly or delete section.

## KNOWN GENERIC/FAKE REMNANTS (verify each still present, then remove/replace)
1. src/lib/mockData.ts exports still rendered anywhere: MOCK_PROMO_CODES suggested codes 'WELCOME20','FASHION15','FREESHIP' clickable chips in app/cart/page.tsx (~line 393-412) — remove chips + validatePromoCode usage entirely (promos aren't real; strip promo UI block from cart incl. appliedPromo state, discount payload fields).
2. MOCK_PICKUP_STATIONS / MOCK_LOCAL_DELIVERY_OPTIONS drive shipping UI in cart — replace shipping selector with a simple free-text "Delivery notes (area, estate, landmark)" textarea; remove pickup/local selectors, their cost math, and fulfillment_mode/pickup_station/local_delivery_option payload fields (server never prices them anyway). Keep delivery_address.text + phone.
3. vendors/[id]/page.tsx: hardcoded "Member Since 2024" → use vendor created_at year; Policies tab shows identical fabricated shipping/returns policy for every vendor → DELETE the Policies tab; compliance_score shown as star "Rating" in one place and "Compliance" elsewhere → label consistently "Compliance score" once, or drop display.
4. app/page.tsx home: fake avatar circles (A/B/C initials people), any remaining quantified claims — replace with real platform facts (categories count from API, live product count if already fetched) or plain value statements; decorative dead "Pay with M-Pesa" button → non-interactive visual (span/img role presentation).
5. marketing-content.ts: scan for leftover invented personas/places; keep only true statements.
6. Any "Powered by Vercel"/template strings, lorem, TODO/user-facing dev notes — grep and clear.
7. SizeGuide modal hardcoded to clothing on all products (products/[id], QuickViewModal) — hide size-guide entry unless product category name matches clothing|shoes|accessories.
8. SearchAutocomplete: navigates to /marketplace?search= — confirm marketplace hydrates ?search= (it does via location.search); also wire arrow-key/Enter selection (onKeyDown) — small.

## BUGS ACROSS STATES (fix)
9. Dark-mode hardcoded light classes sweep: grep for `divide-gray-`, `bg-gray-[12]`, `bg-green-50`, `border-green-200`, `bg-yellow-50`, `bg-red-50`, `text-gray-[456]00` in src/app + src/components — replace with token equivalents (var(--surface-muted), var(--border), var(--brand-wash), var(--text-secondary) etc.). Prioritize customer journey: home, marketplace, products/[id], cart, vendors/[id], wishlist, compare, login/signup, account/orders, orders track.
10. NaN guards: Math.round(v.compliance_score) renders "NaN%" when null ((app)/admin/compliance ~105, account/orders ~150, products/page ~84 KES NaN from ?? fallback dividing undefined cents) — guard with Number.isFinite checks + em-dash fallback.
11. Empty/loading states: ensure every async page has explicit empty state with next-action CTA (marketplace no-results → "No products yet in this category" + link to /vendors; vendors empty; wishlist already ok; account/orders empty ok). fetchError stored-but-unrendered in marketplace (~59) → render inline error banner with Retry.
12. Focus visibility: interactive cards/buttons using outline:none anywhere → restore :focus-visible ring token.
13. QuickViewModal: reset internal state per product open (parent key or useEffect on productId), lock body scroll while open, Escape closes.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Match existing code style exactly; Tailwind tokens via CSS vars as used throughout.
- Do NOT touch apps/api or apps/mobile. Do NOT change routes or add dependencies.
- Homepage layout structure stays recognizable — evolve copy/content within existing sections rather than rebuilding layout.
- After all edits: npm install already done (node_modules present). Build must pass green. Report: files changed one-liner each, build tail output, anything skipped+why, and a list of every banned-word/generic string you removed.
